'''Bernard Berrian''' (born December 27, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State Bulldogs]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Berrian - Minnesota Vikings Wide Receiver |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/5603/bernard-berrian |access-date=December 14, 2023 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2001. Berrian was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the third round of the [[2004 NFL draft]]. He also played in the NFL for the [[Minnesota Vikings]].

==Early life==
Berrian was born in [[Spain]],<ref>{{cite news|first=Chip|last=Scoggins|title=Relatively speedy will do for Vikings|date=July 27, 2008|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/25946144.html?page=1&c=y|work=Star Tribune|access-date=August 26, 2009|archive-date=December 27, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227195344/https://www.startribune.com/sports/25946144.html?page=1&c=y|url-status=dead}}</ref> and grew up in [[Winton, California]], while both of his parents served at [[Castle Air Force Base]]. Berrian attended [[Atwater High School]] in [[Atwater, California]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Berrian Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BerrBe00.htm |access-date=December 17, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> where he played football and basketball and ran track. He was named Modesto Bee player of the year in 1998. Cal High All-Northern California team member. He was known as an explosive two-way starter for Atwater High School, which went 13–1 his senior year, after he caught 53 passes for 1,276 yards and 16 [[touchdowns]]. In [[track & field]], he competed in the 200- and 400-meter dashes, recording times of 22.6 in the 200m and 50.6 in the 400m.

===Chicago Bears===
The [[Chicago Bears]] selected Berrian with the 78th pick in the third round of the [[2004 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/draft.htm |title=2004 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=May 6, 2023}}</ref>

Berrian spent a majority of his early years with the Bears as a back-up wide receiver and return specialist. His playtime increased during the [[2005 Chicago Bears season]], but an injury kept him sidelined for a portion of the season. Berrian returned to play during the Bears' NFC Divisional game against the [[Carolina Panthers]], but eventually he was forced to leave after sustaining an injury.

During the early half of the [[2006 Chicago Bears season]], Berrian emerged as one of the Bears's most productive receivers and sharpest deep-threat weapons. On November 5, 2006, Berrian suffered an injury to his ribs during a game against the [[Miami Dolphins]]. According to Berrian, he sustained the injury after hitting the ground during the very first play of the game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.suntimes.com/sports/mulligan/125578,CST-SPT-mside06.article |title=Berrian out 2–4 weeks with rib injury |access-date=December 14, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081011142843/http://www.suntimes.com/sports/mulligan/125578,CST-SPT-mside06.article |archive-date=October 11, 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Berrian returned from the injury after missing only one game, but struggled at times. His surrogate, [[Mark Bradley]], momentarily became the Bears' deep threat. Berrian finished the regular season as the Bears' second leading wide receiver, only a few catches behind team leader [[Muhsin Muhammad]].<ref>[https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/chi2006.htm 2006 Chicago Bears Statistics]</ref>

During the [[2006–07 NFL playoffs|2006 playoffs]], in the divisional round game against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], Berrian caught five passes for 105 yards, including a 68-yard touchdown pass. The [[Chicago Bears]] went on to win 27–24 in overtime. In the NFC championship game against the [[New Orleans Saints]], Berrian led the Bears with five receptions for 85 yards. He also made a clutch, 33-yard diving touchdown reception behind a jumping [[Fred Thomas (NFL player)|Fred Thomas]], giving the Bears an eleven-point lead, which contributed to their 39–14 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/recap;_ylt=Ah20Hvo9GZRY3X_tBs_RaFFDubYF?gid=20070121003| title= Super Bowl reshuffle: Bears back on top of NFCl}}</ref> Well after the season's conclusion, the catch was named one of the Bears' top ten plays in 2006.<ref>Chicagobears.com, [http://www.chicagobears.com/Top10Plays.asp Top 10 Plays of 2006] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090819044928/http://www.chicagobears.com/Top10Plays.asp |date=August 19, 2009 }} Retrieved on March 22, 2007</ref> Berrian played in [[Super Bowl XLI]] against the [[Indianapolis Colts]], where he caught four passes for 38 yards.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=270204003 Indianapolis Colts vs. Chicago Bears - Box Score - February 04, 2007 - ESPN]</ref> Berrian was in the last year of his contract and the Bears chose not to put a franchise tag on him. The Bears had to wait until the Free Agency period on February 29, 2008, for Berrian to become an unrestricted free agent and negotiate a new contract.
[[File:20090104 Brian Dawkins (20).JPG|thumb|left|250px|Berrian (top right, 87) and [[Brian Dawkins]] in January 2009.]]

===Minnesota Vikings===
On March 1, 2008, Berrian signed a six-year, $42 million contract with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] that included $16 million in guaranteed money.

His first touchdown as a Viking was against the [[New Orleans Saints]] which tied up the game 27–27 they would later win that game 30–27. He led all wideouts with 102 yards off a career playoff-high nine catches. He also caught an 86-yard catch and run against the Lions. On November 30, 2008, in a game against the [[Chicago Bears]], Berrian caught a 99-yard touchdown pass from [[Gus Frerotte]], tying an NFL record for the longest pass from scrimmage. On December 14, 2008, he returned an 82-yard punt against the [[Arizona Cardinals]] after a quick three and out on their opening drive. He also caught a 49-yard touchdown pass in a 28–21 victory over the [[Houston Texans]]. Berrian had the highest average per. catch that NFL season with 20.1 yards per catch. Berrian finished the season with 48 catches, 964 yards and 7 touchdowns. (50 catches for exactly 1,000 yards and 7 touchdowns including the playoffs.)
In 2009, with the acquisition of 20-year veteran quarterback [[Brett Favre]], Berrian became one of the deep threats of the wide receiver core along with [[Sidney Rice]], [[Percy Harvin]], and [[Visanthe Shiancoe]]. He struggled with a hamstring injury that bothered him all season long. He ended the season with 55 catches for 618 yards and 4 touchdowns, 2 touchdowns in the series with the [[Green Bay Packers]], and 2 in the games with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] and [[Baltimore Ravens]]. In the NFC Championship, Berrian recorded 9 receptions for 102 yards.

In 2010, the 7-year veteran finished with 28 receptions, for 252 yards, and no touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bernard Berrian 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BerrBe00/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=2025-08-04 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> It was his lowest season in his entire career. His best performance of the season came against the Arizona Cardinals where he caught 9 passes for 91 yards.

On October 24, 2011, Berrian was released by the Vikings.<ref>{{cite web | title=Vikings cut ties to embattled WR Berrian after four seasons | website=NFL.com | date=2011-10-25 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/vikings-cut-ties-to-embattled-wr-berrian-after-four-seasons-09000d5d82377aca | access-date=2025-08-04}}</ref>

==Charity work==
In November 2008, Bernard pledged to donate up to $10,000 to Second Harvest Heartland, Minnesota's largest hunger-relief organization, to provide turkeys to hungry inner-city families for the holiday season. He donated $5,000 to Second Harvest Heartland to provide turkeys to local inner-city families for Thanksgiving.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://blog.2harvest.org/tag/bernard-berrian/ |title=Hunger Matters |access-date=July 22, 2009 |archive-date=October 8, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008030559/http://blog.2harvest.org/tag/bernard-berrian/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
Berrian has expressed interest in participating in additional community outreach programs.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/article/pressRelease/idUS210032+24-Nov-2008+PRN20081124 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120910151010/http://www.reuters.com/article/pressRelease/idUS210032+24-Nov-2008+PRN20081124 | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 10, 2012 | work=Reuters | title=Vikings Wide Receiver Bernard Berrian Pledges Up to $10,000 to Second Harvest Heartland | date=November 24, 2008 }}</ref>

Berrian was a contestant on [[NBC]]'s [[Minute to Win It]] on September 7, 2010, where he was playing to win money for the Second Harvest Heartland.<ref>{{cite web | title=NBC's 'Minute to Win It' to Air Special NFL Themed Episodes September 7 & 8 Leading Up to NBC's NFL Kickoff on September 9 | website=TheFutonCritic.com | date=2010-08-19 | url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2010/08/19/nbcs-minute-to-win-it-to-air-special-nfl-themed-episodes-september-7-and-8-leading-up-to-nbcs-nfl-kickoff-on-september-9/20100819nbc01/ | access-date=2026-03-10}}</ref>

==Personal life==
During a [[Monday Night Football]] appearance, [[Muhsin Muhammad]] revealed that Berrian's nickname is "B-twice". However, in a later interview with [[WFLD|Fox News Chicago]], Berrian stated his teammates also call him, "California Cool".<ref>[http://www.myfoxchicago.com/myfox/pages/Sports/Detail?contentId=2066986&version=1&locale=EN-US&layoutCode=VSTY&pageId=6.1.1 MyFox Chicago | Bears Receiver Bernard Berrian on the Game] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070117211534/http://www.myfoxchicago.com/myfox/pages/Sports/Detail?contentId=2066986&version=1&locale=EN-US&layoutCode=VSTY&pageId=6.1.1 |date=January 17, 2007 }}</ref> ChicagoBears.com's columnists and announcers also refer to Berrian as the "Silent Assassin".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.myfoxchicago.com/myfox/pages/Sports/Detail?contentId=2136349&version=1&locale=EN-US&layoutCode=VSTY&pageId=6.1.1 |title=Bernard Berrian: The Day After |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080106175504/http://www.myfoxchicago.com/myfox/pages/Sports/Detail?contentId=2136349&version=1&locale=EN-US&layoutCode=VSTY&pageId=6.1.1 |archive-date=January 6, 2008 }}</ref> He is friends with [[Chad Johnson (wide receiver)|Chad Johnson]] and appeared occasionally on his dating show [[Ochocinco: The Ultimate Catch]].

In 2015, Berrian was inducted into the Fresno County Athletic Hall of Fame.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fresnoahof.org/current-past-inductees|title=Fresno County Athletic Hall of Fame {{!}} Home|website=Fresno County Athletic Hall of Fame {{!}} Home|access-date=February 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170731195939/https://www.fresnoahof.org/current-past-inductees|archive-date=July 31, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Tyron Lamar "Bennie" Anderson''' (born February 17, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee State Tigers football|Tennessee State Tigers]].

==High school and college careers==
Anderson attended [[Cleveland Junior Naval Academy]] in [[St. Louis, Missouri]] where he was an all-district performer.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=ANDERBEN01|title= Bennie Anderson|publisher= databaseFootball.com|accessdate= November 10, 2012|url-status= usurped|archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20121017013400/http://databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=ANDERBEN01|archivedate= October 17, 2012}}</ref>

He was a four-year letterman at Tennessee State<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/A/AndeBe20.htm|title= Bennie Anderson |publisher= Pro-Football-Reference.Com |accessdate= November 10, 2012}}</ref> (1996–99) where he started 43 of the 45 games in which he played during his career. He was a first-team All-[[Ohio Valley Conference]] pick as both a junior and senior, when he also earned the school's leadership award by the “Tree Coaches” (Tennessee State alumni coaches who sit under a tree watching practice).He was a first-team Black College [[All-America]] pick as a senior in 1999.

==Professional career==

===2000===
Anderson was initially signed by the [[St. Louis Rams]] in 2000 as an undrafted rookie [[free agent]]. He was waived by the team on July 19 and spent rest of the year out of football.

===2001===
Anderson resurfaced with the Chicago Enforcers of the now defunct [[XFL (2001)|XFL]] in the spring of 2001. He started at right guard for the Enforcers the entire season, paving the way for former [[NFL]] running backs [[LeShon Johnson]] and [[John Avery (gridiron football)|John Avery]] (also a former first-round pick by the Miami Dolphins).

Later that year, Anderson would go on to play in all 16 regular season games with 13 starts at right guard for the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. After seeing action in a reserve role in the first two regular season games, he made the first start of his NFL career at the [[Denver Broncos]] on September 30 as the Ravens rushed for 112 yards and the line did not allow a sack in a 20–13 victory. Anderson also opened both playoff games.

===2002===
Anderson started all 16 games at right guard for the Ravens in 2002. He was one of only three Ravens offensive players to start all 16 games that year. He was part of a line that led the way for a running game that averaged 112.0 yards per contest and put together a 4.2-yard average per attempt as [[running back]] [[Jamal Lewis (American football)|Jamal Lewis]] rushed for 1,327 yards and reached the 100-yard rushing mark in five games.

===2003===
Anderson opened all 15 regular season games in which he played at right guard for the Ravens in 2003. He dressed but did not play in the finale against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].  He was part of a line that paved the way for Jamal Lewis, who put together the second-best individual rushing performance in NFL history with 2,066 yards. Anderson also opened first-round playoff game against the [[Tennessee Titans]] on January 3, 2004.

===2004===
In his final season with the Ravens, Anderson played in all 16 contests, including 12 starts at right guard. He also saw action at left guard during the course of the season. He was an integral part of a line that led a running game which averaged 128.9 yards per contest and allowed 2.2 sacks an outing. Behind the line, running backs Jamal Lewis (4) and [[Chester Taylor]] (2) combined for six 100-yard rushing games.

===2005===
After the Ravens signed free agent offensive guard [[Keydrick Vincent]] from the Pittsburgh Steelers in early 2005, it became clear they had no interest in re-signing Anderson. He signed with the Buffalo Bills on March 19. The contract was a three-year deal worth $5.1 million. It also featured a $400,000 bonus if he met certain playing-time incentives.

Anderson started 15 of the 16 games in which he appeared at left guard for the Bills. The only game he did not open was against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on November 13, when he was replaced by [[Mike Williams (offensive lineman)|Mike Williams]] after struggling with pass protection. Anderson re-assumed the role after Williams was injured on November 27. During the year, Anderson was part of a line that led the way for running back [[Willis McGahee]], who compiled his second straight 1,000-yard rushing season with 1,247 yards.

===2006===
Anderson was expected to have the edge on the starting left guard position for the Bills in 2006, but was waived by the team on June 9. On June 15, he signed a to a two-year contract with the Miami Dolphins. The move reunited him with [[Mike Mularkey]], who was the head coach for the Bills in 2004 and 2005 before becoming the offensive coordinator in Miami.

He initially assumed the starting right guard job after injuries to [[Seth McKinney]] and rookie [[Joe Toledo]]. Anderson started the first two games of the regular season at right guard before being injured on September 17 against his former team, the Buffalo Bills. The injury, which proved to be a torn triceps, landed Anderson on Injured Reserve. He was replaced by [[Kendyl Jacox]] and later [[L. J. Shelton]] at right guard.

==Personal life==
Bennie is married with four sons: Bennie Jr, Joshua, Joseph, and Jeremiah. Bennie Jr. and Joshua are offensive linemen at [[Yale University]] and [[Eastern Michigan University]] respectively, and Joseph has committed to play defensive line at the [[University of Iowa]].

Anderson earned a degree in history at Tennessee State, where he subsequently obtained his teaching certificate. He currently works as a history teacher at [[Westminster Christian Academy (Missouri)|Westminster Christian Academy]].

'''Benjamin Seth Watson'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Watson Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WatsBe00.htm |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> (born December 18, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils football|Duke Blue Devils]] and [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]]. Watson was selected by the [[New England Patriots]] with the 32nd overall pick in the first round of the [[2004 NFL draft]] and won [[Super Bowl XXXIX]] with the Patriots in his rookie year.  He also played in the NFL for the [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Baltimore Ravens]], and [[New Orleans Saints]].

==Early life==
Watson was born in [[Norfolk, Virginia]]. He attended [[Northwestern High School (Rock Hill, South Carolina)|Northwestern High School]] in [[Rock Hill, South Carolina]], and was a letterman in football and track. In football, as a senior, he caught 31 passes for 515 yards. The two-time All-Region selection and Northwestern HS Student of the Year led his team to the state championship in his junior season. He was also a member of his high school chapter of The [[Fellowship of Christian Athletes]].

In [[track and field]], Watson was a standout sprinter, recording personal-best times of 22.37 seconds in the [[200 meters]] and 50.03 seconds in the [[400 meters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/ben-watson-3333/|title=Ben Watson - Arkansas State - Patriots TE|access-date=January 27, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202032616/https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/ben-watson-3333/|archive-date=February 2, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Watson played football at [[Duke University]] prior to transferring to the [[University of Georgia]] where he majored in [[finance]]. In 3 seasons at Georgia, he had 65 catches for 852 yards and 6 TD.

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Watson attended the NFL combine and completed all of the combine and positional drills. He scored a 48 on the [[Wonderlic test]], tying for the third highest score of any player in league history.<ref name="bleacherreport">{{Cite web |last=Schmidt |first=Jeffrey |date=April 4, 2012 |title=2012 NFL Draft: The 5 Best, 5 Worst Wonderlic Scores in NFL History |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1130834-nfl-draft-2012-the-5-best-and-the-5-worst-wonderlic-scores-in-nfl-history/page/4#/articles/1130834-nfl-draft-2012-the-5-best-and-the-5-worst-wonderlic-scores-in-nfl-history/page/4 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120424053658/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1130834-nfl-draft-2012-the-5-best-and-the-5-worst-wonderlic-scores-in-nfl-history/page/4#/articles/1130834-nfl-draft-2012-the-5-best-and-the-5-worst-wonderlic-scores-in-nfl-history/page/4 |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 24, 2012 |access-date=2025-02-02 |website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> On March 18, 2004, Watson participated at [[2003 Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia's pro day]], but chose to stand on his combine numbers and only performed positional drills and the 40-yard dash. Team representatives and scouts from every team attended, including head coaches [[Mike Sherman]] [[Green Bay Packers|(Packers)]] and [[Butch Davis]] [[Cleveland Browns|(Browns)]]. His overall performance impressed scouts and solidified his position as a top tight end in the draft.<ref>{{cite web |title=Watson impressed on Pro Day |url=https://247sports.com/college/georgia/Article/Watson-impresses-on-Pro-Day-104078141/ |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=247sports.com |author=Legge, Dan |date=March 18, 2004}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Watson was projected to a second round pick by NFL draft experts and scouts. He was ranked the third best tight end prospect in the draft by DraftScout.com.<ref>{{cite web |title=Benjamin Watson, DS #3 TE, Georgia |url=http://www.draftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=1967&draftyear=2004&genpos=te |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=draftscout.com}}</ref>

===New England Patriots (first stint)===
==== 2004 season ====
The [[New England Patriots]] selected Watson in the first round (32nd overall) of the [[2004 NFL draft]]. Watson was the second tight end drafted in 2004, after [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami's]] [[Kellen Winslow II]] (seventh overall).<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/draft.htm |title=2004 NFL Draft Listing |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref>

Watson held out of training camp and missed 18 days due to a contract dispute. On August 14, 2004, Watson fired his agent Tom Condon, but was contractually obligated to retain [[IMG (company)|IMG]] as his representative.<ref>{{cite web |title=Patriots' holdout fires his agent |url=http://www.thesunchronicle.com/sports/patriots-holdout-fires-his-agent/article_d971dc90-dad1-5ccc-add2-ba52b48f92be.html |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=thesunchronicle.com |author=Farinella, Mark |date=August 14, 2004}}</ref> On August 16, 2004, the New England Patriots signed Watson to a six-year, $13.50 million contract that included a [[signing bonus]] of $3.81 million.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pats Rookie Ends Holdout, Signs On |url=https://www.courant.com/2004/08/17/pats-rookie-ends-holdout-signs-on/| access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |author=Greenberg, Alan |date=August 17, 2004}}</ref><ref name="spotrac">{{cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Benjamin Watson contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/new-orleans-saints/benjamin-watson-4602/ |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref><ref name="overthecap">{{cite web |title=Overthecap.com: Benjamin Watson contract |url=https://overthecap.com/player/ben-watson/1483 |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=overthecap.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Watson competed against [[Daniel Graham]] to be the starting tight end. Head coach [[Bill Belichick]] officially named Watson the starting tight end to begin the regular season in 2004. He made his NFL debut and first start in the Patriots' season-opener against the [[2004 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] and caught two passes for 16 yards in their 27–24 win, but was inactive for the Patriots' Week 2 win at the [[2004 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]] and was placed on injured reserve for the rest of the season due to a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hopes High for Tight End Benjamin Watson |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/new-england-patriots/Article/Hopes-High-For-Tight-End-Ben-Watson-104238577/ |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=247sports.com}}</ref> During his absence, the New England Patriots finished first in the [[AFC East]] with a 14–2 record and reached the [[Super Bowl]] after defeating the Colts 20–3 in the AFC Divisional Round and the [[2004 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] 41–27 in the AFC Championship Game. Watson received a [[Super Bowl ring]] after the Patriots defeated the [[2004 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] 24–21 in [[Super Bowl XXXIX]].

==== 2005 season ====
Watson returned as the Patriots' primary starting tight end in 2005. On October 9, 2005, Watson scored his first NFL touchdown off of a 33-yard pass by quarterback [[Tom Brady]] as the Patriots defeated the [[2005 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] 31–28 in Week 5. In Week 11, he caught a season-high four passes for 66 receiving yards during a 24–17 victory against the [[2005 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]]. On December 11, 2005, Watson caught three passes for 35-yards before exiting in the fourth quarter of the Patriots' 35–7 victory at the [[2005 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] after suffering a [[concussion]]. He remained inactive for their Week 15 victory against the [[2005 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref name="injury">{{cite web |title=Sports Injuring Predictor: Benjamin Watson |url=https://sportsinjurypredictor.com/player/benjamin-watson/3155 |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=sportsinjurypredictor.com |archive-date=August 10, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810042613/https://sportsinjurypredictor.com/player/benjamin-watson/3155 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Watson finished the 2005 season with 29 receptions, 441 receiving yards, and four touchdown receptions in 15 games and nine starts.<ref name="career"/>

The Patriots finished the 2005 season atop the AFC East with a 10–6 record and qualified for the playoffs. On January 7, 2006, Watson started his first career playoff game and recorded five receptions for 91 yards and scored on a 63-yard touchdown reception as the Patriots defeated the [[2005 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the AFC Wildcard Game. The following week, they were eliminated during a 27–13 loss at the [[2005 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] in the AFC Divisional Round.<ref name="stats5">{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2005) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2005 |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> During the game, Watson ran the distance of the football field to catch and tackle [[Champ Bailey]] at the Broncos' one-yard line after an interception in the Patriots' end zone, preventing a touchdown. The play has been called "one of the greatest forgotten plays in Patriots history."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boston.com/sports/new-england-patriots/2016/12/15/ben-watson-champ-bailey-tackle-2006-video/|title=Remembering one of the greatest forgotten plays in Patriots history|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref>

==== 2006 season ====
Watson entered the season as the Patriots' starting tight end. On October 30, 2006, Watson caught a season-high seven passes for 95-yards and a touchdown during a 31–7 win at the [[2006 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] in Week 8. In Week 14, he sustained a knee injury during a 21–0 loss at the [[2006 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] and was sidelined for the last three games of the season (Weeks 15–17).<ref>{{cite web |title=Patriots-Titans Injury Report |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/new-england-patriots/Article/Patriots-Titans-Injury-Report-104387371 |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=247sports.com}}</ref>

He finished the [[2006 NFL season|2006 season]] with 49 receptions for 643 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 13 regular season games and 13 starts.<ref name="career"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Reiss |first=Mike |date=March 12, 2010 |title=Source: Watson gets $12M from Browns |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=4988424 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

The Patriots finished first in the AFC East with a 12–4 record and reached the AFC Championship before losing at the [[2006 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] 38–34. During that game, Watson caught five passes for 48 yards, his best performance of the playoffs.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2006) |url= http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2006 |access-date= August 9, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

==== 2007 season ====
Watson remained the primary starting tight end for the Patriots in 2007.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: New England Patriots Depth Chart: 09/02/2007 |url= http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/17/NE |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On October 7, 2007, Watson caught six passes for a season-high 107 receiving yards and two touchdowns during a 34–17 win against the [[2007 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] in Week 5. This became Watson's first multi-touchdown performance and first game with over 100 receiving yards.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 5-2007: Cleveland Browns @ New England Patriots |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2007100702/2007/REG5/browns@patriots#tab=recap |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Watson sustained an ankle injury and was inactive for two games (Weeks 7–8).<ref name="injury"/> During his absence he was replaced by [[Kyle Brady]]. Watson was inactive for another two games (Weeks 15–16) after aggravating his sprained ankle.<ref name="injury"/>

Watson finished the 2007 season with 38 receptions for 389 receiving yards and a career-high six touchdown receptions.<ref name="career"/> The Patriots finished atop the AFC with a 16–0 record. On January 12, 2008, Watson caught two passes for 12-yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots' 31–20 win against [[2007 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the AFC Divisional Round. They reached the Super Bowl after defeating the [[2007 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] 21–12 in the AFC Championship Game. On February 2, 2008, Watson started in [[Super Bowl XLII]], but was held without a reception as the Patriots lost 17–14 to the [[2007 New York Giants season|New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2007) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2007 |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

==== 2008 season ====
Watson again started at tight end for the Patriots in 2008.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: New England Patriots Depth Chart: 08/31/2008 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/29/NE |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Watson sustained a knee injury during the preseason and was sidelined for the first two regular season games (Weeks 1–2).<ref>{{cite web |title=Brady's three-year streak on injury reported comes to an end |url=https://archive.boston.com/sports/articles/2008/09/06/bradys_three_year_streak_on_injury_report_comes_to_an_end/ |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=archive.boston.com |date=September 6, 2008}}</ref> On November 13, 2008, Watson caught a season-high eight receptions for 88-yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 34–31 loss to the [[2008 New York Jets season|New York Jets]] in Week 11.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2008) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2008 |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Watson finished the season with 22 receptions, 229 receiving yards, and 2 touchdowns in 14 games and nine starts. Watson's performance was limited, in part, due to an injury to Tom Brady that sidelined him for the entire season. With Brady sidelined with a torn ACL, the Patriots started backup [[Matt Cassel]] and finished with an 11–5 record, but did not qualify for the playoffs.<ref name="career"/>

==== 2009 season ====
[[File:Benjamin Watson 2009.jpg|upright|thumb|left|Watson in 2009]]
Watson retained his role as the primary Patriots tight end and became the only returning tight end after the Patriots released David Thomas and signed free agents [[Chris Baker (tight end)|Chris Baker]] and [[Michael Matthews (American football)|Michael Matthews]]. He started the Patriots' season-opener against the [[2009 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] and recorded a season-high six receptions for 77-yards and caught two touchdown passes during a 25–24 victory.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2009) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2009 |access-date=August 9, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

He finished the [[2009 NFL season|2009 season]] with 29 receptions for 404 receiving yards and five touchdowns in 16 games and seven starts.<ref name="career"/> The Patriots finished atop the AFC East with a 10–6 record but lost in the first round of the playoffs, 33–14 to the [[2009 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]].

Watson became an unrestricted free agent for the first time in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=Watson leaves with mixed emotions |url=http://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/columns/story?columnist=reiss_mike&id=4992578 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |author=Reiss, Mike |date=March 15, 2010}}</ref>

On March 12, 2010, the [[Cleveland Browns]] signed Watson to a three-year, $12 million contract with $6.35 million guaranteed.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Free Agency: Ben Watson Signs 3 YR/$12 Contract With The Browns |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/361540-nfl-free-agency-ben-watson-signs-3-yr12-contract-with-the-browns |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810112701/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/361540-nfl-free-agency-ben-watson-signs-3-yr12-contract-with-the-browns |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 10, 2018 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=BleacherReport.com |author=Rollins, Nathan |date=March 12, 2010}}</ref> He was reunited with Cleveland Browns' head coach [[Eric Mangini]] and offensive coordinator [[Brian Daboll]]. Mangini had been the Patriots' defensive coordinator in 2006 and Daboll had been their wide receiver coach from 2002 to 2006.

===Cleveland Browns===
==== 2010 season ====
[[File:Ben Watson tackled 2012.jpg|thumb|right|Watson (far left) in Browns training camp in 2012]]
Watson started for the Browns throughout the 2010 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Cleveland Browns Depth Chart: 09/05/2010 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/111/CLE |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On September 26, 2010, Watson caught five passes for 47-yards and scored his first touchdown as a member of the Browns during a 24–17 loss at the [[2010 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 1-2010: Cleveland Browns @ Baltimore Ravens |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2010092604/2010/REG3/browns@ravens |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 5, 2010, Watson recorded a season-high ten receptions for 100 receiving yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 13–10 win at the [[2010 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] in Week 13. It marked his first game with double-digit receptions.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2010) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2010 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Watson started in all 16 games for the first time in his career in [[2010 NFL season|2010]] and recorded 68 receptions for 763 receiving yards and three touchdown receptions.<ref name="career"/> Watson led the team in receptions, receiving yards, and tied wide receiver [[Brian Robiskie]] for most receiving touchdowns.

==== 2011 season ====
The Browns fired head coach [[Eric Mangini]] and his staff after the Browns finished with a 5–11 record in 2010.<ref>{{cite web |title=Browns fire Mangini; Holmgren doesn't totally dismiss coaching |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d81d6d737/article/browns-fire-mangini-holmgren-doesnt-totally-dismiss-coaching |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110104235408/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/09000d5d81d6d737/article/browns-fire-mangini-holmgren-doesnt-totally-dismiss-coaching |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 4, 2011 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On July 30, 2011, Watson suffered a concussion after taking an inadvertent knee to the helmet during the Browns' first practice in training camp. Head coach [[Pat Shurmur]] retained Watson as the No. 1 starting tight end on the Browns' depth chart to begin the regular season. On September 25, 2011, he recorded five receptions for a season-high 64-yards during a 17–16 win against the [[2011 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] in Week 3. The following week, Watson caught a season-high six passes for 48 receiving yards and a touchdown as the Browns lost to the [[2011 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]] 31–13. On October 23, 2011, Watson exited the Browns' 6–3 victory against the [[2011 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] at the beginning of the third quarter due to a [[concussion]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2011 |title=Browns lose two to head injuries |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7140935/cleveland-browns-mohamed-massaquoi-benjamin-watson-leave-game-head-injuries |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In Week 14, he caught two passes for 11-yards, but suffered his third concussion of the season and exited in the second quarter of a 14–3 loss at the [[2011 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2011) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2011 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Browns tight end Benjamin Watson done for season after suffering third concussion since training camp |url=https://www.ohio.com/akron/writers/browns-tight-end-benjamin-watson-done-for-season-after-suffering-third-concussion-since-training-camp |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=Ohio.com |date=August 17, 2011}}</ref> On December 16, 2011, the Cleveland Browns officially placed Watson on injured reserve, and he missed the remaining three games of the regular season after being evaluated by a head trauma specialist.<ref>{{cite web |title=Browns Place Ben Watson On IR; FB Eddie Williams Activated |url=https://cleveland.cbslocal.com/2011/12/16/browns-place-ben-watson-on-ir-williams-activated/ |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=cleveland.cbslocal.com |date=December 16, 2011}}</ref>

Watson finished the [[2011 NFL season|2011 season]] with a total of 37 receptions for 410 receiving yards and two touchdowns in 13 games and 11 starts.<ref name="career"/>

==== 2012 season ====
Watson started for the Browns throughout the 2012 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Cleveland Browns Depth Chart: 09/01/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/135/CLE |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> In Week 11, Watson recorded four receptions for 47-yards and caught a season-high two touchdown passes in a 23–20 overtime loss at the [[2012 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 11-2012: Cleveland Browns @ Dallas Cowboys |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2012111804/2012/REG11/browns@cowboys |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 2, 2012, he caught six passes for a season-high 80 receiving yards during a 20–17 win at the [[2012 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] in Week 13. In Week 17, he collected a season-high seven receptions for 64-yards as the Browns lost 24–10 at the [[2012 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2012) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2012 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Watson completed the [[2012 NFL season|2012 season]] with 48 receptions for 501 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 16 games and 14 starts.<ref name="career"/>

===New Orleans Saints (first stint)===
==== 2013 season ====
On March 18, 2013, the [[New Orleans Saints]] signed Watson to a three-year, $4.95 million contract with $1.80 guaranteed and a signing bonus of $1.20 million.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref name="overthecap"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/03/18/saints-sign-ben-watson/|title=Saints sign Ben Watson|date=March 18, 2013|access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref>

Watson entered the Saints training camp slated as a backup for the first time in his career.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: New Orleans Saints Depth Chart: 09/05/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/NO |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Playing behind [[Jimmy Graham]], Watson caught his first touchdown as a member of the Saints in week four on a four-yard pass by quarterback [[Drew Brees]] during a 38–17 win against the [[2013 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]]. On October 13, 2013, he collected three receptions for a season-high 61 receiving yards during a 30–27 loss at the [[2013 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2013) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2013 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was inserted in the starting lineup against the Patriots due to an injury to Jimmy Graham. In Week 10, Watson sustained a [[concussion]] in the Saints' 49–17 win against the [[2013 Dallas Cowboys|Dallas Cowboys]]. He remained inactive for their Week 11 victory against the [[2013 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=New Orleans Saints' Kenny Vaccaro, Benjamin Watson officially out vs. San Francisco |url=https://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2013/11/new_orleans_saints_kenny_vacca_2.html |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=Nola.com |date=November 15, 2013}}</ref>

Watson finished his first season with the Saints with 19 receptions for 226 receiving yards and two touchdowns in 15 games and seven starts.<ref name="career"/>

==== 2014 season ====
Watson returned as the Saints' secondary receiving tight end option behind Jimmy Graham in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: New Orleans Saints Depth Chart: 09/01/2014 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/162/NO |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On October 5, 2014, Watson recorded a season-high five receptions for 43-yards during a 37–31 victory against the [[2014 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in Week 5. In Week 13, he caught a season-long 15-yard pass from Drew Brees in the Saints' 35–32 victory at the [[2014 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2014) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2014 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Watson finished the season with 20 receptions for 136 receiving yards and two touchdowns in 16 games and eight starts.<ref name="career"/>

==== 2015 season ====
[[File:Saints vs Panthers 12.6.15 167.jpg|thumb|right|Watson playing for the Saints in [[2015 New Orleans Saints season|2015]].]]
Watson entered the Saints season as the starting tight end after the departure of Jimmy Graham. Entering the season, Watson was elected an offensive team captain.<ref>{{cite web |title= Ourlads.com: New Orleans Saints Depth Chart: 09/01/2015 |url= http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/175/NO |access-date= August 10, 2018 |website= Ourlads.com}}</ref><ref>Katherine Terrell, [http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2015/09/new_orleans_saints_vote_three.html "New Orleans Saints vote three new captains for 2015 season"], ''[[The Times-Picayune]]'', September 10, 2015.</ref>

In Week 6, Watson caught ten passes for 127-yards and a touchdown during a 31–21 victory against the [[2015 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]]. Writing about that game on [[Thursday Night Football]], one columnist wrote, "it should forever be remembered as The Ben Watson Game, as the 12-year veteran did his best [[Jimmy Graham]] impression with 10 catches and 127 yards and a touchdown. It was cool to watch one of the league's longtime good guys put up a random career game in his 12th season."<ref>Gregg Rosenthal, [https://www.nfl.com/news/saints-knock-out-falcons-from-ranks-of-undefeated-0ap3000000558276 "Saints knock out Falcons from ranks of undefeated"], [[NFL.com]], October 16, 2015 ("It should forever be remembered as The Ben Watson Game, as the 12-year veteran did his best [[Jimmy Graham]] impression with 10 catches and 127 yards and a touchdown. It was cool to watch one of the league's longtime good guys put up a random career game in his 12th season.")</ref>

On November 1, 2015, Watson recorded nine receptions for a season-high 147 receiving yards and a touchdown in the Saints' 52–49 win against the [[2015 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] in Week 8.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Watson started in all 16 games in [[2015 NFL season|2015]] and caught a career-high 74 passes for 825 receiving yards and six touchdowns.<ref name="career"/>

At the conclusion of the 2015 season, Watson was recognized as one of three finalists (with Eli Manning and Anquan Boldin (winner)) for the [[Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award]], honoring a player's volunteer and charity work as well as excellence on the field, and was named an alternate to the Pro Bowl.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/nfl/story/new-orleans-saints-benjamin-watson-walter-payton-man-of-the-year-award-012516|title=Benjamin Watson named a finalist for NFL Man of the Year - FOX Sports|date=January 25, 2016|access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
==== 2016 season ====
On March 9, 2016, the [[Baltimore Ravens]] signed Watson to a two-year, $7 million contract with $3 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $2 million.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Agree-To-Deal-With-TE-Benjamin-Watson/8b27bb8c-be0e-4834-8ef5-d7955295b9b3|title=Ravens Agree To Deal With TE Benjamin Watson|website=www.baltimoreravens.com|access-date=March 10, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/baltimore-ravens/benjamin-watson/|title=Benjamin Watson|last=Spotrac.com|website=Spotrac.com|access-date=March 10, 2016}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Watson competed to be the starting tight end against [[Crockett Gilmore]], [[Dennis Pitta]], and [[Maxx Williams]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Baltimore Ravens Depth Chart: 06/01/2016 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/184/BAL |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> On August 27, 2016, during the Ravens' third preseason game, he suffered a torn Achilles tendon, ending his season.<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ravens-ben-watson-out-for-season-with-torn-achilles-0ap3000000691275|title= Ravens' Ben Watson out for season with torn Achilles|first= Conor|last=Orr|date=August 27, 2016|access-date= August 28, 2016}}</ref>

==== 2017 season ====
During training camp, Watson competed to be the starting tight end against Crockett Gilmore, [[Nick Boyle]], and Maxx Williams.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Baltimore Ravens Depth Chart: 08/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/198/BAL |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref> Head coach [[John Harbaugh]] named Watson the backup tight end on the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind Nick Boyle.<ref>{{cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens release Week 1 depth chart |url=https://www.baltimorebeatdown.com/2017/9/6/16257880/baltimore-ravens-release-week-1-depth-chart |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=BaltimoreBeatdown.com |author=Mazza, Evan |date=September 6, 2017}}</ref> In Week 2, he recorded a season-high eight receptions for 91-yards during the Ravens' 21–10 victory against the [[2017 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]]. On December 17, 2017, Watson caught four passes for 74 receiving yards and caught a 33-yard touchdown pass during a 27–10 win at the Cleveland Browns in Week 15.<ref>{{cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benjamin Watson (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=August 10, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Watson finished the [[2017 NFL season|2017 season]] with 61 receptions for 522 receiving yards and four touchdowns in 16 games and 12 starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benjaminwatson/2506122/careerstats|title=Benjamin Watson: Career Stats at NFL.com|website=[[NFL.com]]|language=en|access-date=January 21, 2018}}</ref> On January 21, 2018, Watson was once again named a finalist for the Walter Payton Man of the Year Award (won by [[J. J. Watt]]).<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nfl.com/manoftheyear|title=NFL Man Of The Year|work=NFL.com|access-date=January 21, 2018|language=en}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints (second stint)===
Watson became an unrestricted free agent after completing his two-year contract with the Baltimore Ravens.

On March 28, 2018, the Saints signed Watson to a one-year, $2 million contract that includes a signing bonus of $645,000.<ref name="spotrac"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Saints sign Benjamin Watson|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/03/28/saints-sign-benjamin-watson/|author=Alper, Josh|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=March 28, 2017}}</ref> On October 21, 2018, Watson caught [[Drew Brees]]' 500th career touchdown pass in a 24–23 win over the [[2018 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]].

That season, Watson won the [[Bart Starr Award]] as the NFL player who "best exemplifies outstanding character and leadership in the home, on the field, and in the community."<ref name=BEN/>

On December 27, 2018, Watson announced that he would be retiring after 15 seasons in the NFL.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001004682/article/saints-te-benjamin-watson-to-retire-at-end-of-season |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228123447/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001004682/article/saints-te-benjamin-watson-to-retire-at-end-of-season |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 28, 2018 |title=Saints TE Benjamin Watson to retire at end of season |first=Adam |last=Maya |website=[[NFL.com]] |date=December 27, 2018 |access-date=May 10, 2019}}</ref>

===New England Patriots (second stint)===
On May 10, 2019, Watson came out of retirement and signed with the Patriots, the team that had originally drafted him back in 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-te-ben-watson-sign-seven-2019-draft-selections |title=Patriots Sign TE Ben Watson; Sign Seven 2019 Draft Selections |website=Patriots.com |date=May 10, 2019 |access-date=May 10, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=New England Patriots sign TE Benjamin Watson|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-england-patriots-sign-te-benjamin-watson-0ap3000001030393|author=Teope, Herbie|website=NFL.com|date=May 9, 2019}}</ref>

On May 27, 2019, Watson announced that he had failed a test for performance-enhancing drugs. In March, during his retirement, his physician had prescribed a testosterone supplement. The NFL responded by suspending Watson for the season's first four games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bromberg |first=Nick |date=May 26, 2019 |title=New Patriots TE Ben Watson facing 4-game NFL suspension for failed drug test |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/new-patriots-te-ben-watson-facing-4-game-nfl-suspension-for-failed-drug-test-222119621.html |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> Watson made his 2019 debut on October 21 in a [[Monday Night Football]] matchup against the [[Jets-Patriots rivalry|rival]] [[New York Jets]] which the Patriots won 33–0. He recorded three catches for 18 yards. Against the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the [[Wild card (sports)|Wild Card]] round, Watson recorded 3 catches for 38 yards as the Patriots lost 20–13.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Tennessee Titans at New England Patriots - January 4th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202001040nwe.htm |access-date=2024-12-24 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Watson announced his second retirement from football on March 16, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/BenjaminSWatson/status/1239581506114387969|title=pic.twitter.com/qvJRDBQIlf|last=Watson|first=Benjamin|date=2020-03-16|website=@BenjaminSWatson|access-date=2020-03-16}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Watson is married to Kirsten Vaughn Watson, who grew up in [[Baton Rouge]].<ref name="for saints1">{{cite web|title=watson family| work=Benjamin Watson| date=August 15, 2013| url=http://www.thebenjaminwatson.com/2013/watson-family-faith-come-first}}</ref> Vaughn was a multisport athlete at [[Episcopal High School (Baton Rouge, Louisiana)|Episcopal High School]].  Her grandfather, Isaac Greggs, was the longtime band director at [[Southern University]].  Her father Percy Vaughn, is from New Orleans and a Southern University graduate.<ref name="for saints1"/>  Her mom, Audree, attended [[Louisiana State University]].<ref name="for saints1"/>

Vaughn and Watson married in 2005 after his rookie NFL year. Together they have seven children, including one set of twins.<ref>{{cite web|title=For Saints tight end Watson, family, faith come first|url=http://theadvocate.com/sports/saints/6747550-123/for-saints-tight-end-watson|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130825222534/http://theadvocate.com/sports/saints/6747550-123/for-saints-tight-end-watson|archive-date=August 25, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thebenjaminwatson.com/2013/watson-family-faith-come-first/|title=Watson: "Family, faith come first" - Benjamin Watson|work=Benjamin Watson |date=August 15, 2013|access-date=January 27, 2017}}</ref> In 2013, Watson said he became a [[Christianity|Christian]] at the age of five or six.<ref>{{cite web |first=Bryce|last=Johnson|title=Unpackin' It — Benjamin Watson|url=http://www.sportsspectrum.com/articles/2013/11/12/unpackin-it-benjamin-watson/|date=November 12, 2015|website=sportsspectrum|access-date=October 17, 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190106153305/https://sportsspectrum.com/featured-article-homepage/2013/11/12/unpackin-it-benjamin-watson/|archive-date= 6 January 2019}}</ref>

Benjamin has a younger brother, Asa, who was signed by the New England Patriots on May 10, 2014, but was released before the season started.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 14, 2014 |title=The Cowboys have reportedly signed the brother of Benjamin Watson |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2014/08/14/cowboys-sign-tight-end-asa-watson |access-date=January 27, 2017 |newspaper=Sports Illustrated}}</ref>

Following the events in Ferguson, Missouri, Watson wrote a Facebook post on the issue of race in America that was "liked" on Facebook more than 850,000 times. The post received national attention.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2014/11/saints_benjamin_watson_ferguso.html|title=Read what Saints' Benjamin Watson wrote on Facebook about unrest in Ferguson, Mo.|access-date=January 27, 2017|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190107015742/https://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2014/11/saints_benjamin_watson_ferguso.html|archive-date= 7 January 2019}}</ref>

On November 17, 2015, Watson released a book, ''Under Our Skin: Getting Real About Race--And Getting Free From the Fears and Frustrations That Divide Us'', with [[Tyndale House Publishers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://mmqb.si.com/mmqb/2015/11/20/nfl-ben-watson-new-orleans-saints-book-under-our-skin|title=Saints TE Ben Watson goes deep with new book on race in U.S. - The MMQB with Peter King|first=Jenny|last=Vrentas|newspaper=Sports Illustrated |date=November 20, 2015 |access-date=January 27, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190106204527/https://www.si.com/mmqb/2015/11/20/nfl-ben-watson-new-orleans-saints-book-under-our-skin|archive-date= 6 January 2019}}</ref>

Watson [[United States anti-abortion movement|opposes abortion]] and spoke at the [[March for Life (Washington, D.C.)|March for Life]] in 2017 and 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://insider.foxnews.com/2017/01/27/nfl-star-benjamin-watson-march-life-his-pro-life-stance|title= NFL Star Ben Watson on March for Life: 'The Pre-Born Are Important| website=Fox News Insider|date= January 28, 2017|access-date= October 17, 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210129125124/http://insider.foxnews.com/2017/01/27/nfl-star-benjamin-watson-march-life-his-pro-life-stance|archive-date= 29 January 2021}}</ref> In 2020, he [[Executive producer|executive produced]] and partially financed a movie called ''Divided Hearts of America'' on the topic of abortion featuring former [[President of the United States|Presidential candidate]] [[Ben Carson]] and niece of [[Martin Luther King Jr.]], [[Alveda King]].<ref name="DHOA">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/patriots-benjamin-watson-producing-abortion-documentary-1270926/|title=Patriots' Benjamin Watson Producing Abortion Documentary|first1=Paul|last1=Bond|date=January 21, 2020|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210914230433/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/patriots-benjamin-watson-producing-abortion-documentary-1270926/|archive-date= 14 September 2021}}</ref>

In 2018, Watson won the [[Bart Starr Award]] as the NFL player who "best exemplifies outstanding character and leadership in the home, on the field, and in the community."<ref name=BEN>{{cite web|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/31812800/sec-network-adds-benjamin-watson-studio-lineup |title= SEC Network adds Benjamin Watson to studio lineup|last1=ESPN PR|date=July 18, 2021|website=SEC Sports/ESPN|access-date=October 17, 2021|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211017065002/https://www.secsports.com/article/31812800/sec-network-adds-benjamin-watson-studio-lineup|archive-date= 17 October 2021}}</ref>

Beginning in 2021, Watson serves as a college football studio analyst for the [[SEC Network]] of [[ESPN Inc.|ESPN]] appearing as a staple on the network's SEC Now and SEC Football Final programs, as well as appearing on the SEC Network's live coverage of the SEC Kickoff program.<ref name=BEN/>

'''Benjamin Dempsey Olson''' (born June 5, 1975) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] for 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 1996. He was selected by the [[Tennessee Oilers]] in the fifth round of the [[1998 NFL draft]] and played his entire career with the Tennessee organization.

==Early life==
Olson was born in [[Bremerton, Washington]]. He attended [[South Kitsap High School]] in [[Port Orchard, Washington]], and was a letterman in [[high school football]], [[wrestling]] and [[track and field]] for the South Kitsap Wolves. In football, as a senior, he was named as second-team All-USA selection by ''[[USA Today]]''. In track and field, he was third at the state championship meet as a junior and fourth as a senior.

==College career==
Olson attended the University of Washington and played for the [[Washington Huskies football]] team from 1994 to 1997. As a junior in 1996, he was recognized as a consensus first-team All-American at guard. As a senior in 1997, he was a first-team All-America selection by the Associated Press and the Walter Camp Foundation.

==Professional career==
The Tennessee Oilers selected Olson in the fifth round (139th pick overall) of the 1998 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1998 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1998/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played for the Oilers (later called the Tennessee Titans) from {{NFL Year|1998}} to {{NFL Year|2007}}. After his rookie season, he started every game in which he played, including a total of 140 of the 152 regular season games in which he appeared. In 1999, the Titans made it to [[Super Bowl XXXIV]] in which Olson started. They lost to the [[Kurt Warner]]-led [[St. Louis Rams]].

'''Horatio Benedict Blades Sr.''' (born September 3, 1966) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). A three-time All-Pro, Blades was named to both the [[Detroit Lions 75th Anniversary Team]] and the [[Detroit Lions#Lions All-Time Team|Detroit Lions All-Time Team]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]].

==College career==
Blades played a big part in the [[University of Miami]]'s winning the 1987 [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] National Championship. He also won the [[Jim Thorpe Award]] in that year and, in 2006, was named to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] for his play with the [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami Hurricanes]]. He shares the University of Miami single season interception record with fellow Miami Hurricane [[Sean Taylor]].

During his play at the University of Miami, he and the defensive secondary were nicknamed "Bennie and the Jets," a reference to [[Bennie and the Jets|the song]] by [[Elton John]], for their speed, power, ability, and stand-out defensive play. Blades also was known for taunting and intimidating opposing players.

Blades was interviewed about his time at the University of Miami for the documentary ''[[The U (film)|The U]]'', which premiered December 12, 2009 on [[ESPN]].

Following his graduation from the [[University of Miami]], Blades entered the [[1988 NFL draft]] and was selected in the first round with the third overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1988 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1988/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He spent ten seasons in the NFL. He played for the [[Detroit Lions]] from 1988 to 1996 and the 1997 season with the [[Seattle Seahawks]], teaming up with his older brother, [[wide receiver]] [[Brian Blades]], who also played collegiate football at the University of Miami.

During his time with the Lions, Blades was considered one of the most physical defensive backs in the NFL, even playing as a linebacker in certain passing situations toward the end of his career. Blades is widely considered to be one of the greatest defensive backs in Lions' history.

The Lions selected Blades with the third overall pick in the 1988 NFL Draft, and he went on to earn NFL All-Rookie honors for the 1988 season. He was selected to the Pro Bowl in 1991 - in addition to receiving First-team All-NFL and First-team All-NFC honors. He was the Lions’ Defensive MVP in 1992 and led the team with 78 tackles in 1996.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/det/1996.htm#all_defense| title = 1996 Detroit Lions Statistics & Players {{!}} Pro-Football-Reference.com| website = [[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> He had two 100-tackle seasons in is first two seasons in Detroit.

An underrated professional player, Blades was a key component to the Lions’ defense that helped the team claim two [[NFC Central]] titles, and a berth in the 1991 NFC Championship game. He was a defensive captain for five years in Detroit and his 815 career tackles place him second on the Lions’ all-time list.

'''Benjamin LaShaun Troupe''' (born September 1, 1982) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] for five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the early 2000s.  Troupe played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], earning [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2003.  He was a second-round pick in the [[2004 NFL draft]], and played professionally for the [[Tennessee Titans]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the NFL.

== Early life ==

Troupe was born in [[Swainsboro, Georgia]] in 1982.<ref name="pfrprofile">{{Cite web |title=Ben Troupe Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TrouBe00.htm |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He attended [[Butler High School (Augusta, Georgia)|Butler High School]] in [[Augusta, Georgia]],<ref name=dbfprofile>databaseFootball.com, Players, {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20110708233757/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=TROUPBEN01  Ben Troupe]}}.  Retrieved March 19, 2011.</ref> where he played high school football for the Butler Bulldogs.<ref name=ufprofile>Gatorzone.com, Football History, 2003 Roster, [http://web.gatorzone.com/football/bios.php?year=2003&sub=team&bio=troupe.html  Ben Troupe] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006162309/http://web.gatorzone.com/football/bios.php?year=2003&sub=team&bio=troupe.html |date=October 6, 2011 }}.  Retrieved March 19, 2011.</ref>  Following his senior season, Troupe was a [[PrepStar College Recruiting|PrepStar]] high school All-American and was recognized by the ''[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]'' as one of the top four tight end prospects in the Southeast.<ref name=ufprofile/>

== College career ==

Troupe accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida, where he played for coach [[Steve Spurrier]] and coach [[Ron Zook]]'s [[Florida Gators football]] teams from [[2000 Florida Gators football team|2000]] to [[2003 Florida Gators football team|2003]].<ref name=ufmediaguide>''[http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2011/media_guide.pdf  2011 Florida Gators Football Media Guide] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402035222/http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2011/media_guide.pdf |date=April 2, 2012 }}'', University Athletic Association, Gainesville, Florida, pp. 89, 97, 101, 143–145, 186 (2011).  Retrieved August 31, 2011.</ref>  He finished his college career with sixty-four [[reception (American football)|reception]]s for 958 yards (14.9 yards per catch) and seven [[touchdown]]s.<ref name=ufprofile/>  As a senior team captain in 2003, Troupe was a first-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) selection and received first-team [[All-American]] honors from [[ESPN]], [[Rivals.com]] and ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''.<ref name=ufmediaguide/>  He was also one of the three finalists for the [[John Mackey Award]], recognizing the nation's best college tight end in 2003.<ref name=ufmediaguide/> He was a part of the 2000 SEC Championship Team.

== Professional career ==

The [[Tennessee Titans]] selected Troupe in the second round with the 40th overall pick of the 2004 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2004/draft.htm |title=2004 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2023-05-06}}</ref>  He played tight end for the Titans from {{NFL Year|2004}} to {{NFL Year|2007}},<ref name=nflprofile>National Football League, Historical Players, [http://www.nfl.com/players/bentroupe/profile?id=TRO531860  Ben Troupe].  Retrieved March 19, 2011.</ref> and was nicknamed "Troupe Scadoop" by his Titans teammates.  During his four seasons with the Titans, he made 106 [[reception (American football)|reception]]s for 1,056 yards and seven touchdowns.<ref name=nflprofile/>

Troupe signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on March 6, 2008.  He was released on September 16, after Buccaneers [[tight end]] [[Jerramy Stevens]] returned from suspension.  Three days after his release from the Buccaneers, Troupe was signed by the [[Oakland Raiders]].  He was placed on injured reserve with a foot injury on October 21, and released by the Raiders on November 17.

== Life after football ==

Troupe formerly with ESPN Radio ESPN Coastal Georgia with stations in Brunswick GA and Savannah Ga. Largest ESPN affiliate in the state of Georgia. Co Host of Three and Out with Kevin Thomas and BJ Bennett on the Southernpigskin Radio Network.Published author with True vine Publishing in Nashville Tennessee Uncommon and Unfinished The Ben Troupe Story with BJ Bennett. Founder of The UncommonCru 501C3 Non Profit Enrichment Intrusive Mentoring Program for boys aged 12-18 based in Swainsboro Ga. Speaker. Motivator. Master communicator. Podcaster. Content Creator. Host of 84 Reasons Podcast. Co Host of Winning The Division Podcast. Co Host of The Fan and the End Podcast. Co Host No Weddings In the Fall Podcast. Ordinary Man Living an Extraordinary Life. Sweet Tea and Shade Trees for life.

'''Benjamin Jeffrey Utecht''' (born June 30, 1981) is an American singer and former professional [[American football|football]] player.<ref name="mm">[http://makingmusicmag.com/ben-utecht-march-2012/ ''Making Music'': Ben Utecht, Former Colts Tight End, Turned Professional Singer] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304094831/http://makingmusicmag.com/ben-utecht-march-2012/ |date=March 4, 2016 }}</ref> He played football as a [[tight end]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] and [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the Colts as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2004 after playing [[college football]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]]. He earned a [[Super Bowl ring]] with the Colts in [[Super Bowl XLI]] over the [[Chicago Bears]].

==Early life==
Utecht graduated from Hastings Senior High School in [[Hastings, Minnesota]] where he helped lead the Raiders to a State Semi-Final appearance.

==College career==
Utecht became a four-year [[Starting lineup|starter]] at the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|University of Minnesota]], starting 35 of 44 games and playing in the [[Music City Bowl]].

==Professional career==

===Indianapolis Colts===
He signed as a [[free agent]] with the Colts on April 30, 2004. Utecht did not see much action in the 2004 and 2005 seasons. His best season was the 2006 season, with 37 receptions for 377 yards. In the 2006 postseason, Utecht had 5 receptions for 41 yards. He would then go on to help the Colts win [[Super Bowl XLI]]. In 2007, he caught 31 receptions for 364 yards and a touchdown. Utecht became a [[restricted free agent]] in the 2008 offseason.

===Cincinnati Bengals===
On March 14, the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] signed him to an offer sheet believed to be worth $9 million over three seasons. The Colts had seven days to match the contract and retain Utecht, but the March 21 deadline passed and Utecht became a member of the Bengals. Prior to the start of the 2009 season, Utecht suffered a concussion during practice, which was aired on the HBO Television show "Hard Knocks". On August 31, 2009, Utecht was placed on the injured reserve list for the Cincinnati Bengals. He was released on November 17 with an injury settlement.

===Singing career===
Following his fifth concussion, Utecht ended his football career to focus on a second career in music. He maintained an interest in performing throughout high school, college and his professional football career and had intended to pursue a musical career after football. Utecht has recorded several albums including a Christmas album for which he was nominated for a 2012 Dove Award. He also went on tour in January 2012 and was featured on the cover of the March/April 2012 issue of ''[[Making Music (magazine)|Making Music]]'' Magazine.<ref name=mm/>

==Personal life==
The son of a [[United Methodist Church|Methodist]] Minister,<ref>{{Cite news |last=James |first=Tom |date=December 22, 2007 |title=Singing a Passion for Colts' Punter, Tight End |url=http://www.tribstar.com/sports/local_story_356234147.html |access-date=March 29, 2009 |work=Tribune-Star |archive-date=September 15, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120915054019/http://www.tribstar.com/sports/local_story_356234147.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Utecht recorded an [[Inspirational music]] album, released on May 5, 2009, on [[Sandi Patty]]'s Stylos label.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 24, 2009 |title=Charley Walters: Tayler Hill Harrows Her College Choices Down to Final Four |url=http://www.twincities.com/ci_11988941?source=most_viewed |access-date=March 29, 2009 |work=St. Paul Pioneer Press |publisher=www.twincities.com}}</ref>

His wife, Karyn (Stordahl) of [[Owatonna, Minnesota]], also attended the [[University of Minnesota]] and was [[Miss Minnesota]], 2005. Ben and Karyn are parents to four daughters.<ref>{{Cite news |date=March 24, 2009 |title=Benjamin Utecht |url=http://benutecht.com/BlogNews/tabid/1125/EntryId/127/Welcome-Elleora-Grace.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20110707223820/http://benutecht.com/BlogNews/tabid/1125/EntryId/127/Welcome-Elleora-Grace.aspx |archive-date=July 7, 2011 |publisher=benutecht.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=November 9, 2010 |title=the twins have arrived! Every one is healthy! Katriel Beverlee and Amy Joan, what an amazing experience! |url=https://twitter.com/BenUtecht/status/2153478759649280 |access-date=July 19, 2013 |publisher=twitter.com}}</ref>

===Traumatic brain injury===
Utecht, who suffered five known concussions during his football career, was already experiencing memory loss by late 2011, when he was 30 years old.<ref name="usatoday30.usatoday">{{Cite news |last=Brady |first=Erik |title=Ex-NFL player Benjamin Utecht battling memory loss |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/story/2011-12-20/former-nfl-player-benjamin-utecht-concussions-singer/52123290/1}}</ref> Utecht released his single "You Will Always Be My Girls" in 2014 dedicated to his family in form of a letter to his wife Karyn and his daughters, as Utecht fears that one day that his brain injuries will lead him to not know them.<ref name="star-tribune">{{Cite news |last=Scoggins |first=Chip |date=June 28, 2014 |title=Utecht writes songs for daughters |url=http://www.startribune.com/june-28-2014-utecht-writes-songs-for-daughters/264978281/ |access-date=December 18, 2015 |publisher=Star-Tribune}}</ref>

== Other media ==
Utecht also wrote the book ''Counting the Days While My Mind Slips Away''.<ref>{{Citation |last=ABC News |title='Concussion' and the Serious Impact of Repeated Head Trauma {{!}} ABC News |date=December 18, 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p17cTTHteY4 |access-date=October 4, 2017}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Lee Sapp II''' (born January 20, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2004. He played [[college football]] for the [[Northern Iowa Panthers football|Northern Iowa Panthers]].

Sapp also played for the [[Miami Dolphins]] and [[Minnesota Vikings]].

==Early life==
Sapp attended [[Boyd H. Anderson High School|Boyd Anderson High School]] in Fort Lauderdale, Florida and was a student and a [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[High school football|football]], [[Scholastic wrestling|wrestling]], [[volleyball]], and [[track and field]]. In football, as a senior, he was a first-team All-[[Broward County, Florida|Broward County]] selection and an All-State Honorable Mention selection. Benny Sapp graduated from Boyd Anderson High School in 2000.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Sapp, Boyd Anderson, Cornerback |url=https://247sports.com/player/benny-sapp-71083/ |access-date=July 22, 2025 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref>

==College career==
He appeared in 24 games (15 [[Starting lineup|starts]]) with the [[Northern Iowa Panthers]] and 24 games (20 starts) with the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]].  He was removed from the Iowa Hawkeyes squad in 2002 due to charges of violence.  He racked up 78 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]], six [[interception]]s, 29 [[Pass deflected|passes deflected]] and four forced [[fumble]]s with the Panthers and 104 tackles and three interceptions in two seasons with the Hawkeyes.

==Professional career==
===Kansas City Chiefs===
Sapp was signed by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2004. He played for them until 2007.

===Minnesota Vikings (first stint)===
Sapp signed with the Vikings in 2008. In [[2008 Minnesota Vikings season|2008]] he stepped in to the Vikings starting nickel rotation after [[Charles Gordon (American football)|Charles Gordon]] went down. In 2008, he had 22 tackles along with 2 interceptions. On March 3, 2009, the Vikings re-signed him to a one-year contract. And re-signed him again for a two-year contract on March 9, 2010.

===Miami Dolphins===
Sapp was traded from the Vikings on August 25, 2010, to the [[Miami Dolphins]] for [[Greg Camarillo]]. For the Dolphins Sapp recorded 2 interceptions and had 10 pass deflections in 17 games. On September 12, 2011, during a ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' game against rival [[New England Patriots]], Sapp was stiff-armed by Patriots WR [[Wes Welker]] on a 99-yard touchdown pass. The Dolphins cut Sapp the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Defensive casualty: Miami Dolphins cut Benny Sapp|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/2011/09/14/2405877/defensive-casualty-miami-dolphins.html|work=Miami Herald|date=September 14, 2011}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings (second stint)===
After CB [[Antoine Winfield Sr.|Antoine Winfield]] sustained a season-ending injury, Sapp was signed by the Vikings after a work out. He recorded 25 tackles and three pass deflections across seven games with the Vikings.

'''Bern Orion Brostek''' (born September 11, 1966) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[St. Louis Rams|Los Angeles/St. Louis Rams]] from 1990 to 1997.

==Early life==
Brostek played [[high school football]] for [[Iolani School]] in [[Honolulu]], [[Hawaii]].  Iolani is also known for sending Albert Tufono, Meki Pei and Willie Kava to the [[University of Washington]].

==College career==
Brostek attended the [[University of Washington]] where he [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[College football|football]].  Brostek was one of the top offensive linemen in the nation while at Washington, and received numerous honors during his time there.

His honors included:

* 1988 Rising Award (given to the most outstanding lineman at Washington).
* 1989 John P. Angel Award (given to the most outstanding offensive lineman at Washington).
* 1989 [[Morris Trophy]] (given to the most outstanding lineman in the [[Pac-10]]).
* 1989 [[Pete Gross]] Player of the year Award (given to the most outstanding player at Washington).
