'''Lewis Ben Williams''' (born May 28, 1970) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player. Born in [[Belzoni, Mississippi]], Williams played as a [[defensive lineman]] at the [[University of Minnesota]]. He led the team in sacks for the 1990 and 1991 seasons, and was named as honorable mention to the [[Associated Press]]'s [[1990 All-Big Ten Conference football team]] and a second-teamer on the [[1991 All-Big Ten Conference football team]]; he held the all-time sack record for the Golden Gophers upon graduation.

After college, Williams played in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) for the [[Shreveport Pirates]], where he was named an [[1994 CFL season#1994 Eastern All-Stars|East Division All-Star]] in 1994. Over two seasons in 1994 and 1995, he recorded 15 sacks and 107 tackles. In the 1997 [[NFL Europe|World League]] draft, he was selected second overall with the first pick of by the [[London Monarchs]]. He played for the Monarchs in 1997 and 1998, recording 73 tackles and nine sacks. Williams made his NFL debut for the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in 1998, playing in one game; he spent most of the season as a backup to [[John Randle]], [[Tony Williams (American football)|Tony Williams]], [[Stalin Colinet]], and [[Fernando Smith]]. The following year, he played in three games for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] before returning to the CFL, playing six games for the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] in 2000. Since his retirement, Williams has become the president of the [[National Football League Players Association]] (NFLPA) in Minnesota as well as an active advocate for [[organ donation]].

==Early life and college==
[[File:Ben Williams - Gophers.jpg|thumb|left|Williams played for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]] in college and retired as their career sacks leader.]]
Ben Williams was born on May 28, 1970 in [[Belzoni, Mississippi]],<ref name="Williams emerges as CFL all-star" /> a small town known as the "catfish capital of the world".<ref name="How the catfish capital of the world was hit by an Asian fish flood">{{cite web |last1=Krupnick |first1=Matt |title=How the catfish capital of the world was hit by an Asian fish flood |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2019/apr/10/belzoni-mississippi-catfish-capital-world-asian-fish-flood |website=The Guardian |access-date=April 8, 2025 |date=April 10, 2019}}</ref> He played football at [[Humphreys County High School]], where he was named player of the year.<ref name="Ravens sign defensive lineman" />

In 1988, Williams committed to the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]].<ref name="Henry commits to MSU; Gardner, Tatum shine">{{cite news |title=Henry commits to MSU; Gardner, Tatum shine |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/278299042/ |access-date=April 7, 2025 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=[[Hattiesburg American]] |date=February 8, 1988 |page=3B |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In his [[1990 Minnesota Golden Gophers football team|junior 1990 season]], Williams led the team with six sacks and seven tackles for loss.<ref name="2015 Media Guide">{{cite web |title=2015 Media Guide |website=[[Minnesota Golden Gophers football team|Minnesota Golden Gophers]] |access-date=April 7, 2025 |page=108 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150905143638/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/minn/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2015-16/prospectus/prospectus.pdf |archive-date=September 5, 2015 |url-status=dead | url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/minn/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2015-16/prospectus/prospectus.pdf }}</ref> He was an honorable mention to the [[Associated Press]]'s [[1990 All-Big Ten Conference football team]].<ref name="Leaders Dominate AP All-Big Ten Team">{{cite news |title=Leaders Dominate AP All-Big Ten Team |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=618rAAAAIBAJ&q=ben+williams&pg=PA5&article_id=2372,7602326#v=onepage |access-date=April 7, 2025 | url-access=subscription |agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=The Daily Reporter |date=November 28, 1990 |page=6}}</ref> In his [[1991 Minnesota Golden Gophers football team|senior 1991 season]], he was named as a second-teamer on the [[1991 All-Big Ten Conference football team]]; he recorded 97 tackles and again led the team with six sacks.<ref name="CFL - Pirate Talk">{{cite news |title=CFL - Pirate Talk |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/218027332/ |access-date=April 8, 2025 |work=[[The Times (Shreveport, Louisiana)|The Times]] |date=July 6, 1994 |page=5 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Williams finished his career at Minnesota with 183 total tackles and 13 sacks,<ref name="Ravens sign defensive lineman" /> making him the school's all-time sacks leader at the time.<ref name="Rice sidelined with mystery bug">{{cite news |title=Rice sidelined with mystery bug |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/989210760/ |access-date=April 7, 2025 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=[[The News Virginian]] |date=July 24, 1997 |page=15}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After the end of his collegiate career, Williams spent two years out of football.<ref name="Journey continues for former Gopher">{{cite news |title=Journey continues for former Gopher |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/223237964/ |access-date=April 7, 2025 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=[[St. Cloud Times]] |date=August 8, 1998 |page=24 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) ahead of the 1993 season, but never made it off the practice squad<ref name="Williams emerges as CFL all-star">{{cite news |title=Williams emerges as CFL all-star |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/508276209/ |access-date=April 7, 2025 |agency=[[The Canadian Press]] |publisher=[[Times-Colonist]] |date=August 30, 1995 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> due to a broken leg.<ref name="Big Ben ready to tick for Esks" /> In 1994, he signed with the CFL's [[Shreveport Pirates]], where he spent two years.<ref name="Journey continues for former Gopher" /> In the [[1994 Shreveport Pirates season|1994 season]], Williams played in 16 games, recording 46 tackles and seven sacks. He was named to the [[1994 CFL season#1994 Eastern All-Stars|East Division All-Star team]],<ref name="Two Pirates are chosen as CFL All-Stars">{{cite news |last1=Heitholt |first1=Kent |title=Two Pirates are chosen as CFL All-Stars |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/218076906/ |access-date=April 7, 2025 |work=[[The Times (Shreveport, Louisiana)|The Times]] |date=November 17, 1994 |page=21 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> and was nominated for the CFL's [[CFL's Most Outstanding Defensive Player Award|Defensive Player of the Year]] award.<ref name="Journey continues for former Gopher" /> Williams was one of only two Pirates selected for the All-Star team.<ref name="Two Pirates are chosen as CFL All-Stars" /> ''[[The Canadian Press]]'' said he was "one of the CFL's top defensive linemen" and the "lone shining light on an abysmal defense".<ref name="Williams emerges as CFL all-star" /> The following year, Williams recorded 61 tackles and 8 sacks with the Pirates over 18 games;<ref name="Pro Football Archives">{{cite web |title=Ben Williams Pro Football Stats, Position, College, Draft |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/w/will01650.html |website=Pro Football Archives |access-date=April 7, 2025}}</ref> the franchise folded following the season.<ref name="A season ends, and a franchise fades into dim memory">{{cite news |last1=Robinson |first1=Tom |title=A season ends, and a franchise fades into dim memory |url=https://scholar.lib.vt.edu/VA-news/VA-Pilot/issues/1995/vp951101/11010584.htm |access-date=April 7, 2025 |publisher=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |date=November 1, 1995 |page=C3}}</ref>

Following his time in the CFL, Williams was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in 1996 and the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in 1997. However, he was waived from both teams.<ref name="Journey continues for former Gopher" /> The [[London Monarchs]] of the [[NFL Europe|World League]] selected Williams with their first pick, and the second pick overall, in the 1997 draft.<ref name="Sportsline">{{cite news |last1=Hayes |first1=Mark |title=Sportsline |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1146859796/ |access-date=April 8, 2025 |publisher=[[USA Today]] |date=February 19, 1997 |page=1B |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="1997 World League draft">{{cite web |title=1997 World League draft |url=http://www.worldleague.com/general/facts/00035926.html |website=[[NFL Europe|World League]] |access-date=April 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/19970709131348/http://www.worldleague.com/general/facts/00035926.html |archive-date=July 9, 1997}}</ref> Williams spent two years with the team in the league, a [[minor league]] intended to develop players.<ref name="Williams closing in on NFL dreams">{{cite web |last1=Balaji |first1=Murali |title=Williams closing in on NFL dreams |url=https://mndaily.com/219979/uncategorized/williams-closing-nfl-dreams/ |website=[[Minnesota Daily]] |access-date=April 7, 2025 |date=August 3, 1998}}</ref> Over his two years with the Monarchs, Williams recorded 73 tackles and 9 sacks.<ref name="Pro Football Archives" /> 

Williams was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] ahead of the [[1998 Minnesota Vikings season|1998 season]].<ref name="Journey continues for former Gopher" /> Williams entered training camp playing behind [[John Randle]] and [[Tony Williams (American football)|Tony Williams]] at defensive tackle,<ref name="Williams closing in on NFL dreams" /> but shifted to defensive end in the season, where he backed up [[Stalin Colinet]] and [[Fernando Smith]].<ref name="Journey continues for former Gopher" /> Williams was promoted from the practice squad to the active roster on December 8.<ref name="Cowboys 2001 Media Guide">{{cite web |title=Cowboys 2001 Media Guide |url=https://archive.org/details/cowboys-2001-media-guide-dallas-b/page/118/mode/2up?view=theater |website=[[Dallas Cowboys]] |access-date=April 7, 2025 |date=August 2001}}</ref> He played in one game in the season,<ref name="Pro Football Reference">{{cite web |title=Ben Williams Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WillBe20.htm |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=April 7, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> recording two quarterback pressures.<ref name="Cowboys 2001 Media Guide" /> The [[1999 Philadelphia Eagles season|following year]], Williams signed with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], where he played as a defensive tackle. In three games, he recorded two tackles and a forced fumble.<ref name="Pro Football Reference" />

In the [[2000 Edmonton Eskimos season|2000 season]], Williams returned to the CFL, playing for the [[Edmonton Eskimos]]. He came back to the league to reunite with [[Don Matthews]], who had been his coach during his time with the Saskatchewan Roughriders.<ref name="Big Ben ready to tick for Esks">{{cite news |last1=Ireland |first1=Joanne |title=Big Ben ready to tick for Esks |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/476562729/ |access-date=April 8, 2025 |publisher=[[Edmonton Journal]] |date=September 29, 2000 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He played in six games for the Eskimos, recording seven tackles and two sacks.<ref name="Pro Football Archives" /> Williams would later have short stints with the [[Chicago Bears]] and the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the 2000 and 2001 seasons,<ref name="Cowboys 2001 Media Guide" /> and the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the 2002 season.<ref name="Ravens sign defensive lineman">{{cite web |title=Ravens sign defensive lineman |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/baltimore-ravens/article/ravens-sign-defensive-lineman-104038596/ |website=[[247Sports]] |access-date=April 7, 2025 |language=en |date=August 8, 2002}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Ben Williams Presidential Medal.jpg|thumb|right|Ben Williams being presented the [[President’s Lifetime Achievement Award]].]]
Williams is an advocate for [[kidney disease]] patients and for [[organ donation]]; in 2019, he underwent a [[kidney transplant]] after being on a waiting list for six years.<ref name="Former Gopher Football and Vikings Player Receives Life-changing Kidney Transplant {{!}} University of Minnesota Physicians">{{cite web |title=Former Gopher Football and Vikings Player Receives Life-changing Kidney Transplant {{!}} University of Minnesota Physicians |url=https://mphysicians.org/news/2020/01/03/former-gopher-football-and-vikings-player-receives-life-changing-kidney-transplant |website=University of Minnesota Physicians |access-date=April 7, 2025 |date=January 3, 2020}}</ref><ref name="Former Vikings & Gophers player Ben Williams gives thanks after kidney transplant">{{cite web |last1=Broaddus |first1=Adrienne |date=November 27, 2019 |title=Former Vikings & Gophers player Ben Williams gives thanks after kidney transplant |url=https://www.kare11.com/article/news/local/breaking-the-news/former-vikings-gophers-player-ben-williams-gives-thanks-after-kidney-transplant/89-d7abe53c-0e71-45fc-b668-1926137b313c |access-date=April 7, 2025 |website=[[KARE (TV)|KARE]]}}</ref><ref name="Barely half of Minnesota men are organ donors. A former Vikings player and kidney recipient says that’s not enough." /> Through the philanthropic support of the Ben Williams Foundation, he helped fund eight mobile [[kidney dialysis]] units throughout the [[Mississippi Delta]], including his hometown of Belzoni, Mississippi.<ref name="Former Vikings & Gophers player Ben Williams gives thanks after kidney transplant" /> Since his transplant, Williams received an [[MBA]] from the [[Kelley School of Business]] at the [[Indiana University Bloomington]], and is pursuing a [[Juris Doctor]] degree at [[Columbia Law School]].<ref name="Barely half of Minnesota men are organ donors. A former Vikings player and kidney recipient says that’s not enough.">{{cite web |last1=McWright |first1=Talia |title=Barely half of Minnesota men are organ donors. A former Vikings player and kidney recipient says that's not enough. |url=https://www.twincities.com/2024/10/29/lifesource-organ-donor-campaign-minnesota-men/ |website=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]] |access-date=April 7, 2025 |date=October 29, 2024}}</ref> Williams is the president of the [[National Football League Players Association]] (NFLPA) - Minnesota Chapter.<ref name="Barely half of Minnesota men are organ donors. A former Vikings player and kidney recipient says that’s not enough." /> Williams was awarded with the [[President’s Lifetime Achievement Award]] by [[Joe Biden]].<ref name="Souhan: Somebody else’s kidney gave Ben Williams life. The former Gophers and Vikings player is giving back.">{{cite web |last1=Souhan |first1=Jim |title=Souhan: Somebody else’s kidney gave Ben Williams life. '''Bennie Cordell Logan''' (born December 28, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[nose tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]], earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2012. He was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the third round of the [[2013 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Logan was born in [[Shreveport, Louisiana]] on December 28, 1989, and grew up with seven brothers and sisters.  He attended [[Red River Senior High School]] in [[Coushatta, Louisiana]], where he was a defensive end for four years on the Red River Bulldogs high school football team.  He was named to the Class 2A all-state first team in his junior and senior seasons.  On October 17, 2014, head coach Reginald Prealow retired Bennie's high school number 60 and Bennie was there to accept it.<ref name="LSU">[http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=3659753 "Bennie Logan Bio"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617183258/http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=3659753 |date=June 17, 2016 }}. lsusports.net. July 9, 2012. Retrieved February 13, 2013.</ref>

==College career==
While attending [[Louisiana State University]], Logan played for coach [[Les Miles]]'s [[LSU Tigers football]] team from 2009 to 2012.  After redshirting during the 2009 season, he played three games in 2010 and had five tackles, including 0.5 for a loss. In 2011, he played 14 games and had 57 [[tackle (football move)|tackles]], including 6.5 for a loss, and three [[quarterback sack]]s. He had six tackles, including 1.5 for a loss, and one sack in the [[2012 BCS National Championship Game|BCS Championship Game]] against the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]].<ref name="LSU"/>

In 2012, Logan had 45 tackles, including 5.5 for a loss, and two sacks.<ref name="cbssports">[http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/players/1664945/bennie-logan "Bennie Logan"]. cbssports.com. Retrieved February 13, 2013.</ref> He had a season-high nine tackles in the [[2012 Chick-fil-A Bowl]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/15850/bennie-logan "Bennie Logan"]. espn.go.com. Retrieved February 13, 2013.</ref> He was named an [[All-America]]n by ''[[Pro Football Weekly]]''.<ref>Nawrocki, Nolan. [http://www.profootballweekly.com/2012/12/11/pfw-2012-all-america-team "PFW 2012 All-America team"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130117094819/http://www.profootballweekly.com/2012/12/11/pfw-2012-all-america-team |date=January 17, 2013 }}. profootballweekly.com. December 11, 2012. Retrieved February 13, 2013.</ref> After the 2012 season, Logan declared for the [[NFL draft]].<ref>Batten, Sammy. {{Cite web |url=http://www.fayobserver.com/articles/2013/02/06/1235300?sac=fo.sports |title="South View's Greg Gilmore bound for LSU on Signing day" |access-date=June 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130208011506/http://www.fayobserver.com/articles/2013/02/06/1235300?sac=fo.sports |archive-date=February 8, 2013 |url-status=bot: unknown }}. fayobserver.com. February 6, 2013. Retrieved February 13, 2013.</ref>

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia Eagles===
[[File:Bennie Logan13.jpg|thumb|left|Logan pursues [[2013 Washington Redskins season|Redskins]] quarterback [[Robert Griffin III]] in 2013.]]
Logan was selected fifth in the third round of the [[2013 NFL draft]] (67th overall) by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>Gonzalez, John. [http://www.csnphilly.com/football-philadelphia-eagles/eagles-select-lsu-dt-bennie-logan-third-round "Eagles select LSU DT Bennie Logan in third round"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130429012115/http://www.csnphilly.com/football-philadelphia-eagles/eagles-select-lsu-dt-bennie-logan-third-round |date=April 29, 2013 }}. csnphilly.com. April 26, 2013. Retrieved April 26, 2013.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Logan played 16 games in 2013 and won the starting job 8 games into the season. Logan finished with 27 tackles, 2 sacks, 1 fumble recovery, 2 run stuffs, and a blocked kick.

Logan played and started all 16 games for the Eagles in 2014. Although he did not record a sack, he was recognized as a solid run stopper. He finished with 57 tackles, 1 pass defended, 1 forced fumble, and finished in the top 10 in the NFL in run stuffs, with 8.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportingcharts.com/nfl/stats/stuffs-and-stuff-yards/2014/ | title=Stuffs and Stuff Yards: 2014 NFL Season }}</ref>

2015 was considered a breakout year for Logan. Logan was praised by Eagles fans as a central part of their defense due to his effectiveness in stopping the run. Logan played and started the first 14 games before going down with a knee injury against the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web|title = Eagles place Bennie Logan on injured reserve, promote Randall Evans|url = http://www.nj.com/eagles/index.ssf/2016/01/eagles_place_bennie_logan_on_injured_reserve_promo.html|website = NJ.com|date = January 3, 2016|access-date = December 7, 2016}}</ref> He finished with 55 tackles, 1 sack, and was tied for 8th in the NFL in run stuffs with 10.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.sportingcharts.com/nfl/stats/stuffs-and-stuff-yards/2015/ | title=Stuffs and Stuff Yards: 2015 NFL Season }}</ref>

In 2016, Logan played and started 13 games, totaling 24 tackles, 2.5 sacks, 5 run stuffs, 2 forced fumbles, 1 fumble recovery, and 2 blocked kicks.

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On March 13, 2017, Logan signed a one-year deal worth $8 million with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs signing defensive tackle Bennie Logan|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chiefs-sign-defensive-tackle-bennie-logan-0ap3000000792768|author=Patra, Kevin|website=NFL.com|date=March 13, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bennie Logan, Chiefs Agree on Contract|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2691163-bennie-logan-to-chiefs-latest-contract-details-comments-and-reaction|author=Daniels, Tim|website=BleacherReport.com|date=March 13, 2017}}</ref> He played in 15 games with 12 starts for the Chiefs in 2017, recording 52 tackles and 1.5 sacks.

===Tennessee Titans===
On April 8, 2018, Logan signed a one year, $4 million contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bennie Logan joins Titans on one-year, $4M deal|author=Bergman, Jeremy|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bennie-logan-joins-titans-on-one-year-4m-deal-0ap3000000925522|date=April 8, 2018|access-date=April 8, 2018|website=NFL.com}}</ref> Logan played in 15 games while starting none, finishing the 2018 season with 14 tackles and no sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bennie Logan 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LogaBe00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Bennett Troy Jackson Jr.''' (born September 16, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the sixth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]].

==Early life==
Jackson grew up in [[Hazlet, New Jersey]], where he attended [[Raritan High School]].<ref>Dunleavy, Ryan. [http://www.app.com/story/sports/nfl/giants/2015/05/09/bennett-jackson-hazlet-anew-giants-rookie-mini-camp/27010581/ "Bennett Jackson of Hazlet starts anew in Giants rookie mini-camp"], ''[[Asbury Park Press]]'', May 9, 2015. Accessed May 17, 2015. "Jackson is one of 17 second-year pros among the 66 players in rookie mini-camp with the Giants, though the Raritan High School product has the same amount of regular-season game experience as those new to the NFL."</ref> He recorded 40 receptions for 729 yards and rushed 20 times for 350 yards as senior in 2010. He also played [[defensive back]] and intercepted four passes in 2009, helping lead Raritan to 8–3 record in 2009. He caught 35 passes for 509 yards with four touchdowns during his junior season in 2008 and rushed 35 times for 267 yards and four touchdowns. He added two passing touchdowns, two punt returns for touchdowns and one kickoff return for a score during his junior season, averaging 38 yards per kickoff return and 18 yards per punt return in 2008.

He also competed in track and field as [[sprint (running)|sprinter]] and a [[hurdling|hurdler]]. He was a specialist in the [[110 meter hurdles]], he ran a personal best of 13.75 seconds. He also competed in the [[100 meters]], [[200 meters]] and [[400 meters]], posting personal bests of 10.82 seconds, 21.73 seconds and 49.36 seconds, respectively.

Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], he was rated as the 61st best [[wide receiver]] in the nation.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Bennett-Jackson-95604 Bennett Jackson – Yahoo Sports]</ref> He committed to [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]] over offers from [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]], [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers]] and [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern]].

==College career==
Jackson began his career at [[wide receiver]] playing mostly on special teams as a freshman in 2010. He recorded ten total tackles and had one carry for twenty yards. In 2011, after converting to [[cornerback]] in spring practice,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-02-01 |title=Bennett Jackson moving to defensive back |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/college-football/news/bennett-jackson-moving-to-defensive-back |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> playing mostly on special teams and as a backup, he recorded 18 tackles. In his junior season in 2012, he started all 13 games. He recorded 65 total tackles, including one and a half for loss, four interceptions and four pass break ups while playing the entire season with a torn [[Glenoid labrum|labrum]] in his right shoulder.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.uhnd.com/articles/football/ready-prime-time-13-3-bennett-jackson/ |title=Bennett Jackson excelled as first time starter, despite injury |access-date=August 17, 2013 |archive-date=August 30, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130830005719/http://www.uhnd.com/articles/football/ready-prime-time-13-3-bennett-jackson/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2013, as a senior, he recorded 64 tackles, including five for loss, one sack, one forced fumble, two interceptions and three pass breakups.

==Professional career==
===New York Giants===
Jackson was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the sixth round (187th overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Giants draft CB Bennett Jackson in sixth round|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-draft-CB-Bennett-Jackson-in-sixth-round/fc78a90a-8147-47b0-815d-9d23e0a22ff1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170812174125/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-draft-CB-Bennett-Jackson-in-sixth-round/fc78a90a-8147-47b0-815d-9d23e0a22ff1|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 12, 2017|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=May 10, 2014}}</ref>

Jackson signed his rookie contract with the Giants on May 19, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Giants Sign Odell Beckham Jr., Weston Richburg, Devon Kennard & Bennett Jackson|url=http://www.giants101.com/2014/05/20/new-york-giants-sign-odell-beckham-jr-weston-richburg-devon-kennard-bennett-jackson/|access-date=May 20, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520221338/http://www.giants101.com/2014/05/20/new-york-giants-sign-odell-beckham-jr-weston-richburg-devon-kennard-bennett-jackson/|archive-date=May 20, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was cut on August 30, as part of the roster cutdown to 53 players, but was re-signed to the team's [[practice squad]] the following day. Entering the 2015 season, the Giants announced that Jackson would be moving from cornerback to safety. On August 22, 2015, Jackson suffered a [[anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]] in the Giants' second preseason game and missed the entirety of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2015/08/bennett_jackson_giants_knee_injury.html |title=Giants safety Bennett Jackson has torn ACL in knee |last=Raanan |first=Jordan |date=August 23, 2015 |website=[[NJ.com]] |access-date=August 23, 2015}}</ref> On September 1, he was officially placed on injured reserve by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-first-round-of-roster-cuts/5cabc25f-08bc-49f9-9ddc-88aace127876 |title=New York Giants announce first round of roster cuts |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 1, 2015 |website=Giants.com |access-date=September 1, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918064718/https://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-first-round-of-roster-cuts/5cabc25f-08bc-49f9-9ddc-88aace127876|archive-date=September 18, 2017}}</ref>

On August 30, 2016, Jackson was released by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants announce first round of roster cuts|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-announce-first-round-of-roster-cuts/ba500404-bd0c-4b38-8df3-904858c6d669|last=Eisen|first=Michael|website=Giants.com|date=August 30, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170823071720/https://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-announce-first-round-of-roster-cuts/ba500404-bd0c-4b38-8df3-904858c6d669|archive-date=August 23, 2017}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens (first stint)===
On January 3, 2018, Jackson signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens sign former Giants defensive back Bennett Jackson to reserve/future deal|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bs-sp-bennett-jackson-signs-ravens-20180103-story.html|website=BaltimoreSun.com|date=January 3, 2018|access-date=January 4, 2018|archive-date=January 4, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104002004/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bs-sp-bennett-jackson-signs-ravens-20180103-story.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 31.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Release 10 Players, Send Four to Injured Reserve|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-release-10-players-send-four-to-injured-reserve|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=August 31, 2018}}</ref> Jackson was released by the Ravens on September 6. He was re-signed to the team's practice squad on November 27.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Sign DB Bennett Jackson To P-Squad, Release RB Mark Thompson|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/ravens-sign-db-bennett-jackson-to-p-squad-release-rb-mark-thompson/|work=NFL Trade Rumors|date=November 27, 2018}}</ref> 

Jackson signed a reserve/future contract with the Ravens on January 8, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens sign 8 players to reserve/futures contracts|url=https://ravenswire.usatoday.com/2019/01/08/ravens-sign-8-players-to-reserve-futures-contracts/|work=Ravens Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=January 8, 2019}}</ref> On August 31, Jackson was waived by the Ravens.

===New York Jets (first stint)===
On September 1, 2019, Jackson was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Meet Jets' waiver claims: Who are Kaare Vedvik, Braxton Berrios, John Franklin, Bennett Jackson?|url=https://www.nj.com/jets/2019/09/meet-jets-waiver-claims-who-are-kaare-vedvik-braxton-berrios-john-franklin-bennett-jackson.html|website=NJ.com|date=September 1, 2019}}</ref> He was waived on September 16, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Promote QB Luke Falk to Active Roster|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-promote-qb-luke-falk-to-active-roster|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 16, 2019|access-date=September 17, 2019|archive-date=September 27, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927113249/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-promote-qb-luke-falk-to-active-roster|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens (second stint)===
On October 15, 2019, Jackson was signed by the Baltimore Ravens off of the Jets' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Bring Back Veteran Safety Bennett Jackson|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-bring-back-veteran-safety-bennett-jackson|author=Brown, Clifton|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=October 15, 2019}}</ref> He made four appearances for the Ravens, recording five combined tackles. Jackson was waived by Baltimore on December 2.

===New York Jets (second stint)===
On December 3, 2019, Jackson was claimed off waivers by the New York Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Place C.J. Mosley on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-c-j-mosley-on-injured-reserve|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 3, 2019}}</ref> He made two appearances for the team to close out the year, logging one tackle.

On March 25, 2020, Jackson was re-signed by the Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Re-Sign S Bennett Jackson|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-re-sign-s-bennett-jackson|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=March 25, 2020}}</ref> He was released on September 5, and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Move 27 to Get Their Roster to 53-Player Limit|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-53-man-roster-2020-season|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=15 Signed to Practice Squad; All Were in Jets Training Camp|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-practice-squad-2020-season|author=Lange, Randy|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=September 6, 2020}}</ref> Jackson was promoted to the active roster on November 3.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign LB Bryce Hager, S Bennett Jackson to Active Roster; Release OL Jimmy Murray|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-lb-bryce-hager-s-bennett-jackson-to-active-roster-release-ol-jimmy-mur|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=November 3, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on December 12.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Activate CB Bless Austin, TE Trevon Wesco from Injured Reserve; Place 3 on IR|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-cb-bless-austin-te-trevon-wesco-from-injured-reserve-place-3-on-ir|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 12, 2020}}</ref>

Jackson re-signed with the Jets again on April 8, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |author=Greenberg, Ethan |title=Jets Re-Sign S Bennett Jackson |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-re-sign-s-bennett-jackson-x9945 |website=NewYorkJets.com |date=April 8, 2021 |access-date=April 9, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on August 17.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Waive Three; Place OL Cameron Clark on Injured Reserve|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-waive-three-place-ol-cameron-clark-on-injured-reserve|author=Allen, Eric|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=August 17, 2021}}</ref> Jackson was re-signed on August 20,<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Re-Sign S Bennett Jackson, Place S Zane Lewis on IR|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-re-sign-s-bennett-jackson-place-s-zane-lewis-on-ir|website=newyorkjets.com|access-date=August 21, 2021}}</ref> but was released once more on August 30.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan  |date=August 30, 2021 |title=Jets Trade for Texans DE Shaq Lawson |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-trade-for-texans-de-shaq-lawson |access-date=August 30, 2021 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

'''Benjamin Corey Cunningham''' (born July 7, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders football|Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders]] and was signed by the [[St. Louis Rams]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2013.

==Early life==
Cunningham attended [[Goodpasture Christian School]] in [[Madison, Tennessee]], where he was a letterman in football, basketball, and track.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 4, 2017 |title=Old School Labs Signs Benny Cunningham as Brand Ambassador |url=https://www.oldschoollabs.com/benny-cunningham-brand-ambassador/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613020127/https://www.oldschoollabs.com/benny-cunningham-brand-ambassador/ |archive-date=June 13, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=Old School Labs |language=en-US}}</ref> In [[high school football|football]], he rushed for 721 yards and 16 touchdowns on offense, while collecting 62 tackles and an interception on defense. As a senior, he rushed for a new school record 1,744 yards and 2,357 all purpose yards to go along with 29 [[touchdowns]], leading Goodpasture to the state semifinals. He was named the Tennessee Titans Mr. Football Class 2A Back for 2008, the TSWA All-State and the Region Player of the Year and was voted to the All-Southern Football Team by the Orlando Sentinel.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TSSAA News |url=https://tssaa.org/wp-content/uploads/TSSAANews/Archive/2009Winter.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160803121847/http://tssaa.org/wp-content/uploads/TSSAANews/Archive/2009Winter.pdf |archive-date=August 3, 2016 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=TSSAA}}</ref> He owns the school record in single-season rushing yards (1,744), career touchdowns (60), touchdowns in a game (five), touchdowns in a season (29), and all-purpose yards in a season (2,357) and career (4,611). He was also selected to play at the Tennessee East-West All-Star Game.

Also an standout [[track & field]] athlete, Cunningham was one of the state's top performers in the sprinting events. At the 2009 TSSAA State T&F Championships, he took gold in both the [[100 meters]], with a time of 10.6 seconds, and in the [[200 meters]], at 21.86 seconds. In addition, he competed in the [[800 metres|800 meter run]] event and was a member of the [[4 x 100 metres relay|4 × 100 m relay]] squad. He also recorded a 4.39 [[40-yard dash]] in practice.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benjamin Cunningham – Feed |url=https://tn.milesplit.com/athletes/274064-benjamin-cunningham/feed |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230624202515/https://tn.milesplit.com/athletes/274064-benjamin-cunningham/feed |archive-date=June 24, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=TNMileSplit |language=en}}</ref>

Regarded only as a two-star recruit by the ''[[Rivals.com]]'' recruiting network, Cunningham chose MTSU over scholarship offers from [[Miami RedHawks football|Miami (OH)]] and [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles football|Tennessee Tech]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ben Cunningham, 2009 Athlete, Mid Tennessee |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/ben-cunningham-29066?view=pv |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704163559/https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/ben-cunningham-29066?view=pv |archive-date=July 4, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===St. Louis / Los Angeles Rams===
Cunningham was signed by the [[St. Louis Rams]] as an undrafted free agent in 2013 and made their 53-man roster.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Jim |date=September 1, 2013 |title=Rams running game pops behind new faces |url=http://www.stltoday.com/sports/football/professional/cunningham-gets-nod-from-faulk-for-work-vs-ravens/article_233fc14b-283d-5c99-ac24-0cbf6ee1e277.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130220818/https://www.stltoday.com/sports/football/professional/cunningham-gets-nod-from-faulk-for-work-vs-ravens/article_233fc14b-283d-5c99-ac24-0cbf6ee1e277.html |archive-date=January 30, 2021 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=STLtoday.com}}</ref> For the 2013 season, he carried the ball 47 times for 261 yards (5.6 average) and a touchdown. He added six receptions for 59 yards in a backup role.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Cunningham 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2013/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103004920/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2013/ |archive-date=January 3, 2019 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2014 season, he had 246 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns to go along with 45 receptions for 352 receiving yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Cunningham 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103004923/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2014/ |archive-date=January 3, 2019 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2015 season, he had 37 carries for 140 rushing yards and 26 receptions for 250 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Cunningham 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2015/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180407053905/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2015/ |archive-date=April 7, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Cunningham signed a one-year extension with the Rams on April 6, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McAtee, Joe |date=April 7, 2016 |title=Los Angeles Rams RB Benny Cunningham Re-Signs...Via Snapchat |url=http://www.turfshowtimes.com/2016/4/7/11390532/los-angeles-rams-benny-cunningham-contract |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220180153/http://www.turfshowtimes.com/2016/4/7/11390532/los-angeles-rams-benny-cunningham-contract |archive-date=December 20, 2016 |access-date=December 15, 2016 |website=TurfShowTimes.com}}</ref>

Cunningham was placed on injured reserve on December 15, 2016, with a neck injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McAtee, Joe |date=December 15, 2016 |title=LA Rams Place DE Robert Quinn, RB Benny Cunningham On IR; Promote OL David Arkin, DL Morgan Fox From PS |url=http://www.turfshowtimes.com/2016/12/15/13974402/la-rams-robert-quinn-benny-cunningham-injured-reserve-david-arkin-morgan-fox |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220180142/http://www.turfshowtimes.com/2016/12/15/13974402/la-rams-robert-quinn-benny-cunningham-injured-reserve-david-arkin-morgan-fox |archive-date=December 20, 2016 |access-date=December 15, 2016 |website=TurfShowTimes.com}}</ref> He finished the 2016 season with 21 carries for 101 rushing yards and 16 receptions for 91 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Cunningham 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180407053821/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2016/ |archive-date=April 7, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On March 21, 2017, Cunningham signed with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiltfong |first=Lester A. |date=March 21, 2017 |title=Chicago Bears sign Benny Cunningham |url=http://www.windycitygridiron.com/2017/3/21/15016830/chicago-bears-sign-benny-cunningham-nfl-free-agency-rams |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004233754/https://www.windycitygridiron.com/2017/3/21/15016830/chicago-bears-sign-benny-cunningham-nfl-free-agency-rams |archive-date=October 4, 2022 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=Windy City Gridiron|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

On September 10, 2017, in his Bears debut, Cunningham had one punt return for 23 yards in the 23–17 home loss to the [[2017 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] at [[Soldier Field]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Chicago Bears – September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100chi.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170920021504/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100chi.htm |archive-date=September 20, 2017 |access-date=October 2, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> On October 9, against the [[2017 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]], he had a 38-yard touchdown reception from punter [[Pat O'Donnell]] on a trick play.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 9, 2017 |title=Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710090chi.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329171913/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710090chi.htm |archive-date=March 29, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2017 season with 20 receptions for 240 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Cunningham 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180407053710/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2017/ |archive-date=April 7, 2018 |access-date=April 6, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On April 3, 2018, Cunningham re-signed with the Bears on a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=April 3, 2018 |title=Bears ink Cunningham to one-year deal |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-ink-cunningham-to-one-year-deal-20506201 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230428014504/https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-ink-cunningham-to-one-year-deal-20506201 |archive-date=April 28, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=ChicagoBears.com}}</ref> During the 2018 season, Cunningham recorded 20 rushing yards on 11 attempts and one reception for nine yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=February 5, 2019 |title=Bears 2018 position review: Running back |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-2018-position-review-running-back |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190212011506/https://www.chicagobears.com/news/bears-2018-position-review-running-back |archive-date=February 12, 2019 |access-date=February 11, 2019 |website=[[Chicago Bears]]}}</ref> Overall, in the 2018 season, he had 11 carries for 20 rushing yards to go along with eight kickoff returns for 173 net yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Cunningham 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201123134217/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CunnBe01/gamelog/2018/ |archive-date=November 23, 2020 |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On April 2, 2019, Cunningham signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=April 2, 2019 |title=Official: Cunningham signs |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-cunningham-signs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230426053418/https://www.jaguars.com/news/official-cunningham-signs |archive-date=April 26, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He was released by the Jaguars on August 11.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=August 11, 2019 |title=Jaguars sign Ben Ijalana, release Benny Cunningham |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/08/11/jaguars-sign-ben-ijalana-release-benny-cunningham/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230624202230/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/08/11/jaguars-sign-ben-ijalana-release-benny-cunningham/ |archive-date=June 24, 2023 |access-date=June 24, 2023 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Benson Babatunde Mayowa''' (born August 3, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Idaho Vandals football|Idaho Vandals]]. Mayowa played in the NFL for the [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[Arizona Cardinals]], [[Oakland Raiders]], and [[Seattle Seahawks]].

==Early life and college==
Mayowa attended [[Inglewood High School (California)|Inglewood High School]], where as a senior [[defensive end]], he had 75 tackles, 11 sacks, and one interception, while receiving All-league and second-team all-California Interscholastic Federation honors.

After not being heavily recruited because of his academic grades, he accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Idaho]]. He was a backup [[defensive end]] as a true freshman, registering 6 tackles (2 for loss), one sack and one quarterback hurry. The next year he made 25 tackles (4.5 for loss), 3 sacks, one quarterback hurry, 2 passes defended, 3 forced fumbles and one recovered.

As a junior, he started 6 out of 10 games (missed 2 with an injury), posting 17 tackles (4.5 for loss), 3 sacks, 5 quarterback hurries, 2 passes defended, 2 forced fumbles and one recovered.

As a senior, he started 8 out of 11 games, making 22 tackles (7 for loss), 3 sacks, 4 quarterback hurries, one pass defended and 3 forced fumbles. He finished his college career with 45 games, 67 tackles (47 solo), 11 sacks, 11 forced fumbles, and 3 fumble recoveries.

==Professional career==
[[File:Benson Mayowa.JPG|thumb|left|Mayowa with the Seahawks in 2014]]

===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
On May 13, [[2013 Seattle Seahawks season|2013]], he was signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] as an [[undrafted free agent]], after participating on a tryout basis at their rookie minicamp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Corbin K. |date=2020-04-01 |title=Seahawks Agree to Terms with Veteran DE Benson Mayowa |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/seahawks/news/seahawks-agree-to-terms-with-veteran-de-benson-mayowa |access-date=2024-07-10 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> He played in the first two regular season games and was declared inactive for the rest of the season, as the Seahawks rotated their multiple defensive ends.<ref name="d867">{{cite web | last=Boyle | first=John | title=Seahawks Sign Defensive End Benson Mayowa | website=Seahawks.com| date=2020-04-06 | url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-defensive-end-benson-mayowa | access-date=2025-01-06}}</ref>

On August 30, [[2014 Seattle Seahawks season|2014]], he was waived by Seattle during their final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-08-30 |title=Seattle Seahawks cut-down analysis |url=https://africa.espn.com/blog/seattle-seahawks/post/_/id/8215/seattle-seahawks-cut-down-analysis-5 |access-date=2023-10-07 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders (first stint)===
On August 31, [[2014 Oakland Raiders season|2014]], Mayowa was claimed off waivers by the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Damien |first=Levi |date=2014-08-31 |title=Raiders claim DE Mayowa from Seahawks |url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2014/8/31/6090601/oakland-raiders-claim-de-benson-mayowa-off-waivers-from-seahawks |access-date=2023-10-07 |website=Silver And Black Pride |language=en}}</ref> On December 7, he recorded his first [[NFL]] career sack on quarterback [[Colin Kaepernick]] in a win against the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He finished the season playing in all 16 regular-season games, while starting in 1, with 14 tackles and one sack.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benson Mayowa 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MayoBe00.htm |access-date=2023-10-07 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In [[2015 Oakland Raiders season|2015]], he made 16 tackles, with one sack on [[2015 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] quarterback [[Matthew Stafford]] in a Week 11 loss, as well as one forced fumble and 2 fumble recoveries. He played in 12 games, starting in 2.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benson Mayowa stats |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/gamelog/_/id/16528/benson-mayowa |access-date=March 22, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Benson Mayowa 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MayoBe00.htm |access-date=2023-10-07 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Dallas Cowboys ===
On March 18, [[2016 Dallas Cowboys season|2016]], the [[Dallas Cowboys]] signed Mayowa to a three-year, $8.25 million offer sheet. On March 22, the Raiders declined to match the offer, officially allowing him to sign with the Cowboys without receiving any compensation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |date=March 22, 2016 |title=Cowboys get Mayowa; Raiders decline to match |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/15040913/dallas-cowboys-sign-benson-mayowa-oakland-raiders-decline-match-offer-sheet |access-date=March 22, 2016 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Dallas looked towards Mayowa to provide depth at the [[defensive end]] position, with the looming suspensions to [[DeMarcus Lawrence]] and [[Randy Gregory]], coupled with their decision not to bring back [[Greg Hardy]].

He was placed on physically unable to perform list at the start of training camp, while recovering from a knee scope he underwent in June.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Helman |first=David |date=July 29, 2016 |title=7 Players On PUP/NFI Lists To Start; Escobar & Lawrence Not Among Them |work=Dallas Cowboys |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/07/29/7-players-pupnfi-lists-start-escobar-lawrence-not-among-them |url-status=dead |access-date=March 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309054555/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2016/07/29/7-players-pupnfi-lists-start-escobar-lawrence-not-among-them |archive-date=March 9, 2018}}</ref> He began the season as the starter at right defensive end, until losing his position after Lawrence returned from his four-game suspension. His role began to be reduced and against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], he played less snaps than [[Ryan Davis (defensive end)|Ryan Davis]]. He was declared inactive against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], after being passed on the depth chart by Davis, because he was not providing the pass rush pressure that was expected from him. He was declared inactive against the [[Baltimore Ravens]] and [[Washington Redskins]]. He returned to the lineup against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], experiencing an improvement in his play, while finishing with 6 sacks (led the team), making 4 of them in the last five games.

In [[2017 Dallas Cowboys season|2017]], he was limited at the start of [[Training camp (National Football League)|training camp]] with knee soreness. Even though [[David Irving (American football)|David Irving]], [[Randy Gregory]] and [[Damontre Moore]] where suspended at the beginning of the regular season, Mayowa could not pass [[Tyrone Crawford]] on the depth chart at [[defensive end|right defensive end]]. He suffered a back injury against the [[Oakland Raiders]] and missed the last 2 games. He finished with 21 tackles, one sack, 2 starts and was declared inactive in 2 games.

On March 7, 2018, Mayowa was released by the Cowboys.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Phillips, Rob |date=March 7, 2018 |title=Cowboys Create Cap Space By Releasing DE Benson Mayowa, DT Vellano |url=http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2018/03/07/cowboys-create-cap-space-releasing-de-benson-mayowa-dt-vellano?sf183917055=1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308103323/http://www.dallascowboys.com/news/2018/03/07/cowboys-create-cap-space-releasing-de-benson-mayowa-dt-vellano?sf183917055=1 |archive-date=March 8, 2018 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
[[File:Benson Mayowa 2019.JPG|thumb|Mayowa with the Raiders in 2019]]
On April 23, 2018, Mayowa signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]], to provide depth while [[defensive end]] [[Markus Golden]] recovered from a torn ACL.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban, Darren |date=April 23, 2018 |title=Benson Mayowa Added To Cardinals' Defense |url=http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Benson-Mayowa-Added-To-Cardinals-Defense/782c67b3-c6fc-44e6-84d5-ed222c6f1998 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424135703/http://www.azcardinals.com/news-and-events/article-2/Benson-Mayowa-Added-To-Cardinals-Defense/782c67b3-c6fc-44e6-84d5-ed222c6f1998 |archive-date=April 24, 2018 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref> He played in 15 games with four starts, recording 38 tackles and four sacks.

===Oakland Raiders (second stint)===
On April 12, 2019, Mayowa signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper, Josh |date=April 12, 2019 |title=Raiders signing Benson Mayowa |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/04/12/raiders-signing-benson-mayowa/ |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref>
In Week 1 against the [[2019 Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos]], Mayowa sacked [[Joe Flacco]] twice in the 24-16 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2019 |title=Raiders beat Broncos 24-16 in 1st game after Brown's release |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128025 |access-date=September 9, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In the week 2 defeat to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] he sacked [[Patrick Mahomes]] in the 3rd Quarter <ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.raiders.com/video/mayowa-gets-to-mahomes-for-big-sack | title=Mayowa gets to Mahomes for big sack }}</ref>
In week 5 against the [[Chicago Bears]], Mayowa sacked [[Chase Daniel]] once in the 24-21 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 6, 2019 |title=Josh Jacobs rallies Raiders past Bears 24-21 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128001 |access-date=October 6, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
On April 6, 2020, the [[Seattle Seahawks]] signed Mayowa to a one-year, $3 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=April 6, 2020 |title=Seahawks Sign Defensive End Benson Mayowa |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-defensive-end-benson-mayowa |access-date=June 1, 2020 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> In Week 17 against the [[2020 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]], Mayowa recorded 2 sacks on [[C. J. Beathard]], including a strip sack that was recovered by the Seahawks, during the 26–23 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers - January 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030sfo.htm |access-date=January 7, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 26, 2021, Seahawks re-signed Mayowa to a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Boyle, John |date=March 26, 2021 |title=Seahawks Re-Sign DE Benson Mayowa |work=Seahawks.com |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-re-sign-de-benson-mayowa |access-date=March 27, 2021}}</ref>

On March 17, 2022, Mayowa was released by the Seahawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Release LB Benson Mayowa|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-release-lb-benson-mayowa|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=March 17, 2022}}</ref>

'''Bené Sylvion Benwikere''' ({{IPAc-en|b|ə|ˈ|n|eɪ|_|b|ɛ|n|ˈ|w|ɪ|k|ə|r|i}} {{respell|bə|NAY|_|ben|WIK|ə|ree}}; born September 3, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the fifth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State Spartans]].

==Early life==
Benwikere grew up in [[Los Angeles]]; his father immigrated to the [[United States]] from [[Nigeria]].<ref name="turned corner" /> As a freshman, Benwikere attended [[Los Angeles Unified School District|View Park High School]] and played [[eight-man football]] before transferring to [[Junípero Serra High School (Gardena, California)|Junípero Serra High School]] in [[Gardena, California]].<ref name="SJSU bio">{{Cite web |title=Bené Benwikere |url=https://sjsuspartans.com/sports/football/roster/ben-eacute-benwikere/1058 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016090849/http://www.sjsuspartans.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bene_benwikere_845748.html |archive-date=October 16, 2014 |access-date=August 23, 2020 |publisher=San Jose State Spartans}}</ref> In his first year at Serra, he earned a starting [[cornerback]] spot.  The Serra Cavaliers included future NFL players such as [[Marqise Lee]], [[Robert Woods (wide receiver, born 1992)|Robert Woods]], [[Paul Richardson (American football)|Paul Richardson]], and [[George Farmer (wide receiver, born 1993)|George Farmer]].<ref name="turned corner">{{Cite web |last=Person, Joseph |date=May 22, 2014 |title=Panthers rookie Benwikere's future turned corner in high school |url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2014/05/22/4927204/panthers-rookies-future-turned.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140908165817/http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2014/05/22/4927204/panthers-rookies-future-turned.html |archive-date=September 8, 2014 |access-date=September 8, 2014 |website=Charlotte Observer}}</ref> As a senior, Benwikere helped Serra win the 2009 [[California Interscholastic Federation]] Division 3 title.

A three-sport [[Letterman (sports)|letterwinner]], Benwikere also played [[high school basketball|basketball]] and was a [[sprint (running)|sprinter]] (11.0s in the 100m) and [[long jump|jumper]] on the [[track & field|track]] team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Complete 2008 league results |url=http://w3.lasallehs.org/sports/track/2008%20complete%20drl%20league%20results%20_2_.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303225552/http://w3.lasallehs.org/sports/track/2008%20complete%20drl%20league%20results%20_2_.pdf |archive-date=March 3, 2016 |access-date=February 19, 2017}}</ref><ref name="NFL Combine">{{Cite web |title=Combine Player Profiles: Bene Benwikere |url=http://www.nfl.com/combine/profiles/bene-benwikere?id=2543855 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140525200215/http://www.nfl.com/combine/profiles/bene-benwikere?id=2543855 |archive-date=May 25, 2014 |access-date=September 7, 2014 |publisher=NFL}}</ref>

Benwikere attended football camp at [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]] during high school and had scholarship offers from [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State]], [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State]], [[New Mexico Lobos football|New Mexico]], [[San Diego State Aztecs football|San Diego State]], and [[UNLV Rebels football|UNLV]].<ref name="Scout">{{Cite web |title=Bene Benwikere |url=http://sanjosestate.scout.com/a.z?s=199&p=8&c=1&nid=3779504 |access-date=September 8, 2014 |publisher=scout.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Benwikere committed to [[San Jose State]] on February 2, 2010. He was part of coach [[Mike MacIntyre]]'s first recruiting class at San Jose State, and Benwikere played under MacIntyre from 2010 to 2012 and [[Ron Caragher]] in 2013.

As a [[true freshman]] in 2010, he played in all 13 games and made 9 starts. During his sophomore year, he played in ten games and made two starts. In 2012, Benwikere was named first-team All-[[Western Athletic Conference]] (WAC). He played in 13 games and started 8. Benwikere scored two defensive [[touchdown]]s off a 37-yard [[fumble]] recovery against New Mexico State and 47-yard [[interception]] return against Idaho.<ref name="SJSU bio" /> On November 24 against [[2012 Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football team|Louisiana Tech]], Benwikere tied a San Jose State record with three interceptions.<ref name="draft profile" /> In San Jose State's victory over Bowling Green in the [[2012 Military Bowl]], Benwikere blocked a [[Punt (gridiron football)|punt]] for a [[Safety (gridiron football score)|safety]].<ref name="SJMN summary">{{Cite news |last=Durkin |first=Jimmy |date=December 28, 2012 |title=San Jose State Spartans win Military Bowl 29–20 |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/sjsu-spartans/ci_22269660 |access-date=September 8, 2014 |work=San Jose Mercury News}}</ref>

In his senior season in 2013, Benwikere was named first-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] (MWC), started 11 games, and had a streak of four consecutive games with an interception. In his San Jose State career, Benwikere had 214 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] (including 11.5 for loss), 3 forced fumbles, 2 fumbles recovered (1 returned for touchdown), 14 interceptions (1 returned for touchdown), and 22 [[passes broken up]].<ref name="SJSU bio" /> Benwikere graduated from San Jose State with a B.A. in [[sociology]].<ref>Photo 5 of 85, [http://www.sjsuspartans.com/view.gal?id=160944 San Jose State Athletics 2014 Graduation Participants] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814164924/http://www.sjsuspartans.com/view.gal?id=160944 |date=August 14, 2014 }}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
====2014 season====
The [[Carolina Panthers]] selected Benwikere in the fifth round (148th overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2014/draft.htm |access-date=May 15, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The Panthers traded a fifth (168th overall) and seventh round pick (225th overall) to the [[Minnesota Vikings]] and received a fifth round pick (148th overall) in order to draft Benwikere.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Beversluis, Brian |date=May 10, 2014 |title=NFL Draft 2014: Panthers select CB Bene Benwikere via trade |url=https://www.catscratchreader.com/nfl-draft-3/2014/5/10/5700190/nfl-draft-2014-panthers-select-5th-round-pick |access-date=November 8, 2018 |website=catscratchreader.com}}</ref> Carolina Panthers’ General Manager [[Dave Gettleman]] noted the Panthers’ had graded Benwikere as a fourth round pick.<ref name="turned corner" /> Benwikere was the 19th cornerback drafted in 2014.
[[File:Marlon Brown and Bene Benwikere.jpg|thumb|Benwikere (#25) and [[Marlon Brown]].]]

On May 20, 2014, the Panthers signed Benwikere to a four-year, $2.41 million contract that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $199,000.<ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Bené Benwikere contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/arizona-cardinals/bene-benwikere-14559/ |access-date=November 8, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

As a rookie, during the preseason, Benwikere won the starting [[Nickelback (American football)|nickel corner]] position on the Panther defense over veteran [[Charles Godfrey (American football)|Charles Godfrey]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2014 |title=Newton's protection on right still in doubt |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/carolina-panthers/post/_/id/8299/newtons-protection-on-right-side-remains-unsure |access-date=September 8, 2014 |website=NFL Nation: Carolina Panthers |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On his NFL debut on September 7, 2014, in Carolina's 20–14 win over the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Benwikere had 4 tackles, 1 pass deflection, and a recovery of a forced fumble by teammate [[Luke Kuechly]] on Tampa running back [[Bobby Rainey]].<ref name="Panthers 20 Bucs 14">{{Cite web |title=Panthers 20, Buccaneers 14 |url=http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-20-Buccaneers-14/5c104d48-ea7d-4436-99d9-c300c9e2c756 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518234102/http://www.panthers.com/news/article-2/Panthers-20-Buccaneers-14/5c104d48-ea7d-4436-99d9-c300c9e2c756 |archive-date=May 18, 2017 |access-date=September 8, 2014 |publisher=Carolina Panthers}}</ref><ref name="2014 gamelog">{{Cite web |title=Bene Benwikere Game Log |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benebenwikere/2543855/gamelogs |access-date=September 9, 2014 |publisher=NFL}}</ref> Benwikere's fumble recovery enabled Carolina to [[running out the clock|run out the clock]] en route to their victory.<ref name="Panthers 20 Bucs 14" /> In a week 2 victory over the [[Detroit Lions]], Benwikere allowed only 20% of his targets to catch a pass, had a pressure, and recorded a pass deflection that was nearly picked off by teammate, [[Star Lotulelei]].<ref name="w380">{{cite web | title=Tom Talks: What happened to change Carolina Panthers' stance on Greg Hardy between Friday and Sunday? | website=Raleigh News & Observer | date=2014-09-14 | url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/tom-sorensen/article10060283.html | access-date=2024-10-08}}</ref> Through the first two weeks of the season, [[Pro Football Focus]] (PFF) rated Benwikere as the second best cornerback in the NFL, allowing a completion percentage of only 44.4% of passes thrown in his area.

In the first half of the October 5 game against the [[Chicago Bears]], Benwikere left the game in the first half after twisting his ankle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Jonathan |date=October 6, 2014 |title=Carolina Panthers' no-huddle offense just part of the mix |url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2014/10/06/5224799/carolina-panthers-no-huddle-offense.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110054748/http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2014/10/06/5224799/carolina-panthers-no-huddle-offense.html |archive-date=November 10, 2014 |access-date=November 9, 2014 |website=Charlotte Observer}}</ref> As of November 9, Benwikere has been inactive.<ref name="2014 gamelog" /> In the Panthers week 14 game against the [[New Orleans Saints]], Benwikere recorded his first NFL interception against Saints quarterback [[Drew Brees]]. Despite giving up 8 catches on 10 targets against the Saints, he only gave up 48 yards and his rating when targeted was a 47.1.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2014 |title=Panthers at Saints: Handing Out the Grades |url=https://www.catscratchreader.com/2014/12/8/7356777/panthers-at-saints-handing-out-the-grades |access-date=February 19, 2017}}</ref> Benwikere didn't allow a single touchdown in 254 snaps and 45 targets (best among rookie corners who played at least 25 percent of their team's snaps).<ref name="si.com">{{Cite web |last=Farrar |first=Doug |date=December 23, 2014 |title=Derek Carr, Odell Beckham Jr., Aaron Donald headline All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2014/12/23/best-nfl-rookies-2014-teddy-bridgewater-aaron-donald |access-date=February 19, 2017 |website=SI.com}}</ref> On December 23, 2014, Benwikere was named to the ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' 2014 All-Rookie Team.<ref name="si.com" /> Over the final eight weeks of the regular season, PFF rated Benwikere as the best cover corner in the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |title=P@nthers Tweets before Panthers-Falcons game | NFL Football | the State |url=http://www.thestate.com/2014/12/26/3894815_pnthers-tweets-before-panthers.html?rh%3D1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230005203/http://www.thestate.com/2014/12/26/3894815_pnthers-tweets-before-panthers.html?rh=1 |archive-date=December 30, 2014 |access-date=December 29, 2015}}</ref> During the Panthers playoff victory over the [[Arizona Cardinals]], Benwikere gave up only one reception for 21 yards for the game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 4, 2015 |title=Panthers 27 Cardinals 16: Handing Out the Grades |url=https://www.catscratchreader.com/2015/1/4/7492373/panthers-27-cardinals-16-handing-out-the-grades |access-date=February 19, 2017}}</ref> On January 13, 2015, Benwikere was named to the PFF 2014 All-Rookie Team. He was also named to the All-Rookie teams for both [[ESPN]] and ''Sports Illustrated''. For his rookie season, Benwikere allowed a rookie-low 72.9 opposing quarterback rating, no touchdowns, and was the third best in the NFL in the yards per reception allowed in 459 regular-season snaps.<ref name="j519">{{cite web | last=Farrar | first=Doug | title=NFL draft redux: Reprojecting the first round of the 2014 draft | website=SI.com | date=2015-01-20 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2015/01/20/2014-nfl-draft-redo-derek-carr-odell-beckham-jr-jadeveon-clowney?page=3&devicetype=default | access-date=2025-01-06}}</ref>

====2015 season====
With the Panthers acquisition of [[Charles Tillman]] during the offseason, Benwikere was named the Panthers starting [[Nickelback (gridiron football)|nickelback]] to open the season.<ref name="w360">{{cite web | last=Newton | first=David | title=Bene' Benwikere shows why Panthers' D best with him at nickel | website=ESPN.com | date=2015-06-17 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/carolina-panthers/post/_/id/14169/bene-benwikere-shows-why-panthers-d-best-with-him-at-nickel | access-date=2024-10-23}}</ref> Through the first three weeks of the season, the only two cornerbacks who were targeted 20 or more times and had not allowed a pass for more than 16 yards were Benwikere and teammate, [[Josh Norman (cornerback)|Josh Norman]]. During the Panthers 44–16 victory over the [[Washington Redskins]], Benwikere recorded his first career strip-sack against quarterback [[Kirk Cousins]] and only allowed 14 receiving yards in his zone. On December 13, during a game against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], Benwikere suffered a fractured leg, and was placed on season-ending injury reserve.

On February 7, 2016, Benwikere's Panthers played in [[Super Bowl 50]]. In the game, the Panthers fell to the [[Denver Broncos]] by a score of 24–10.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl 50 – Denver Broncos vs. Carolina Panthers – February 7th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201602070den.htm |access-date=August 7, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref>

====2016 season====
On October 7, Benwikere was released by Carolina after the Panthers defense allowed 300 receiving yards<ref>{{Cite web |last=Orr, Conor |date=October 7, 2016 |title=Struggling Bene' Benwikere cut by Carolina Panthers |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/struggling-bene-benwikere-waived-by-panthers-0ap3000000716960 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> to [[Atlanta Falcons]]' wide receiver [[Julio Jones]] for only the sixth such occurrence in NFL history. Benwikere admitted having some "conditioning issues", allowing the Falcons' Jones to get a step on him.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McClure, Vaughn |date=October 2, 2016 |title=Julio Jones has 300-yard game one week after 1-catch outing |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/17696419/julio-jones-sets-atlanta-falcons-mark-300-yard-game |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>
