'''Benardrick Cornelius McKinney''' (born November 19, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State Bulldogs]] and was selected by the [[Houston Texans]] in the second round of the [[2015 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
A native of [[Tunica, Mississippi]], McKinney attended [[Rosa Fort High School]], where he played [[linebacker]] and [[quarterback]] for the [[Varsity team#North America|varsity]] [[high school football|football]] team and also started for the basketball team. In his junior season, McKinney threw for 530 yards with five [[touchdown]]s and [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushed]] for 100 yards and one score, while also serving as the team's [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]]. On defense, he was credited with 34 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] on the season. As a senior, McKinney accounted for 2,036 total yards of offense and 22 touchdowns (seven on the ground and fifteen passes) with 1,334 passing and 702 yards rushing. He also almost doubled his tackle total with 66. For postseason honors, the state's high school coaches selected him to the North/South All-Star Game as a linebacker.

Regarded as a three-star recruit by [[247Sports.com]], McKinney was ranked as the No. 49 athlete in his class.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benardrick McKinney, Rosa Fort, Athlete |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Benardrick-McKinney-8602/?Institution=14286 |access-date=June 30, 2017 |website=247Sports}}</ref> He was recruited by [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis]], [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Southern Miss]] and [[Mississippi State Bulldogs football|Mississippi State]]. Eventually accepting the Bulldogs' scholarship offer,<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 3, 2011 |title=Tunica's McKinney awarded scholarship |work=Tunica Times |url=http://www.tunicatimes.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1337:tunicas-mckinney-awarded-scholarship&catid=4:sports&Itemid=25}}</ref> McKinney became the first Rosa Fort player to sign with an [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) program since 2001.

== College career ==
[[File:Benardrick McKinney 20141108.jpg|150px|thumb|left|McKinney in 2014]]
After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his initial year at [[Mississippi State University]], McKinney played in all 13 games in the [[2012 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|2012 season]]. By the fourth game, he made the starting lineup and remained there for the rest of the season. A week later at [[2012 Kentucky Wildcats football team|Kentucky]] McKinney posted 12 tackles (10 solo), 1 [[tackle for loss]] and his first two career [[pass breakups]], earning him Co-SEC Freshman of the Week, alongside [[Johnny Manziel]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mississippi State |url=http://www.djournal.com/sports/college/mississippi-state/ |access-date=June 30, 2017 |website=Daily Journal}}</ref> The week after that he recorded a season-high 14 tackles at home against [[2012 Tennessee Volunteers football team|Tennessee]], which he tied later in a loss to [[2012 Texas A&M Aggies football team|Texas A&M]]. For the season, McKinney totalled 102 tackles, which led all SEC freshmen and tied for second among freshmen in the [[Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]]. He earned All-SEC Freshman honors by the SEC coaches and [[ESPN.com]],<ref name="c500">{{Cite web |last=Aschoff |first=Edward |author-link=Edward Aschoff |date=2012-12-12 |title=ESPN.com SEC All-Freshman Team |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/57649/espn-com-sec-all-freshman-team |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> and was named a First-team Freshman [[All-American]] by [[CBSSports.com]], [[FoxSportsNext]], [[Phil Steele]] and [[CollegeFootballNews.com]]. As a sophomore, McKinney led the team in tackles with 71 and sacks with 3.5. As a junior, he again led the team in tackles with 71. He was named first-team All-SEC and was an All-American.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bonner |first=Michael |date=December 11, 2014 |title=Benardrick McKinney earns Walter Camp first-team All-American |url=http://www.clarionledger.com/story/mississippistatesports/2014/12/11/msu-benardrick-mckinney-earns-walter-camp-first-team-all-american/20276957/ |access-date=June 30, 2017 |website=ClarionLedger.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bonner |first=Michael |date=December 17, 2014 |title=Benardrick McKinney earns two more All-American honors |url=http://www.clarionledger.com/story/mississippistatesports/2014/12/17/msu-benardrick-mckinney-all-american-fwaa-sporting-news/20557511/ |access-date=June 30, 2017 |website=ClarionLedger.com}}</ref>

After his junior season, McKinney entered the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref name="h693">{{cite web | last=Scarborough | first=Alex | title=Mississippi State LB McKinney to enter draft | website=ESPN.com | date=2015-01-09 | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2015/story/_/id/12142028/mississippi-state-bulldogs-linebacker-benardrick-mckinney-enter-nfl-draft | access-date=2024-10-29}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
===Pre-draft===
Prior to his junior season, McKinney was projected as a first round selection in the 2015 draft.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Burke |first=Chris |date=October 21, 2014 |title=NFL draft Big Board 2.0: Who stands out in class with no clear frontrunner? |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2014/10/21/2015-nfl-draft-big-board-ranking-marcus-mariota}}</ref> On January 9, 2015, McKinney announced that he had decided to forgo his senior season and enter the draft. Before the start of the pre-draft events, McKinney was ranked as the second best linebacker in the draft by NFL analyst [[Mike Mayock]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=[[Mike Mayock]]. |title=Benardrick McKinney officially declares for NFL Draft |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/mississippistatesports/2015/01/09/msu-benardrick-mckinney-officially-declares-for-nfl-draft/21497311/ |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=clarionledger.com}}</ref> He was one of 34 collegiate linebackers to attend the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]]. McKinney completed all of the essential combine drills and finished second among all linebackers in the [[vertical jump]], fifth in the [[broad jump]], ninth in the [[short shuttle]], tenth in the [[40-yard dash]], and tied for 11th amongst his position group in the [[three-cone drill]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brady, James |date=February 22, 2015 |title=NFL Combine 2015: Full results for linebackers |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2015/2/22/8088097/nfl-combine-2015-full-results-linebackers-paul-dawson |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=sbnation.com}}</ref> On March 4, 2015, he attended Mississippi State's [[pro day]], but opted to stand on his combine numbers and only performed positional drills for the team representatives and scouts from 29 NFL teams, including [[New York Jets]] defensive coordinator [[Kacy Rodgers]] and [[New Orleans Saints]] assistant head coach [[Joe Vitt]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=[[Gil Brandt|Brandt, Gil]] |date=March 4, 2015 |title=New Jets DC, Saints' Vitt on hand to see MSU's top prospects |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-jets-dc-saints-vitt-on-hand-to-see-msu-s-top-prospects-0ap3000000476430 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> As a highly sought after prospect, McKinney attended private visits and workouts with multiple NFL teams, including the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[Miami Dolphins]], [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Cleveland Browns]], [[Denver Broncos]], Saints, [[Chicago Bears]], and [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goessling, Ben |date=April 6, 2015 |title=Rounding up the Minnesota Vikings' pre-draft visits |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/minnesota-vikings/post/_/id/13183/rounding-up-the-vikings-pre-draft-visits |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2015 |title=Dallas Cowboys Pre-Draft Visits: LB Benardrick McKinney and RB Melvin Gordon Scheduled |url=https://www.bloggingtheboys.com/platform/amp/2015/3/18/8247777/dallas-cowboys-pre-draft-visits-lb-benardrick-mckinney-and-rb-melvin-gordon |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=bloggingtheboys.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brady, James |date=April 27, 2015 |title=2015 NFL Draft visit tracker: Which teams are the prospects meeting with? |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2015/3/16/8225465/nfl-draft-2015-visit-tracker-marcus-mariota-jameis-winston |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=sbnation.com}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, McKinney was projected to be a second round pick by draft experts and scouts. He was ranked the third best linebacker in the draft by NFL analyst [[Lance Zierlein]], was ranked the fourth best linebacker by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', was ranked the fifth best inside linebacker by [[Charles Davis (defensive back)|Charles Davis]], and was ranked the fifth best linebacker in the draft by NFL analyst [[Mike Mayock]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis, Charles |date=April 7, 2015 |title=2015 NFL Draft prospect rankings by position |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/2015-nfl-draft-prospect-rankings-by-position-0ap3000000483055 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mike Mayock |title=Mike Mayock's 2015 NFL Draft position rankings 5.0 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/mike-mayock-s-2015-nfl-draft-position-rankings-5-0-0ap3000000488475 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Huguenin, Mike |date=April 23, 2015 |title=2015 NFL Draft positional overviews: Linebackers |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/2015-nfl-draft-positional-overviews-linebackers-0ap3000000487504 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=April 24, 2015 |title=SI's Top 64 Prospects in the 2015 NFL Draft |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/photos/2015/04/24/top-64-prospects-2015-nfl-draft#7 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=si.com}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
====2015====
The [[Houston Texans]] selected McKinney in the second round (43rd overall) of the 2015 draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2015/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-15 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Texans traded to the Browns their second (51st overall), fourth (116th overall), and sixth round (195th overall) picks in the 2015 draft to move up and draft McKinney after receiving the Browns' second (43rd overall) and seventh round (229th overall) picks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sidu, Deepi |date=May 1, 2015 |title=Texans traded up to pick LB Benardrick McKinney |url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-trade-up-to-pick-LB-Benardrick-McKinney/44c95380-72ff-4b3a-a875-db0b43fbea2b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505040752/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-trade-up-to-pick-LB-Benardrick-McKinney/44c95380-72ff-4b3a-a875-db0b43fbea2b |archive-date=May 5, 2015 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=houstontexans.com}}</ref> He was the fourth linebacker selected in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Krollman, Brett |date=May 1, 2015 |title=2015 NFL Draft Results: What Benardrick McKinney Brings To The Texans |url=https://www.battleredblog.com/platform/amp/2015/5/1/8533125/2015-nfl-draft-what-benardrick-mckinney-brings-to-the-texans |access-date=February 25, 2018}}</ref> On May 8, 2015, the Texans signed McKinney to a four-year, $5.34 million contract that includes $2.82 million guaranteed and a [[signing bonus]] of $2.14 million.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Benardrick McKinney contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/houston-texans/benardrick-mckinney-16767/ |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref>

He entered [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]] competing against veterans [[Akeem Dent]], [[Mike Mohamed]], and [[Jeff Tarpinian]] for a job as a starting inside linebacker.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ganguli, Tania |date=June 19, 2015 |title=Jaelen Strong, Benardrick McKinney could start for Houston Texans |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/houston-texans/post/_/id/11515/jaelen-strong-benardrick-mckinney-could-start-for-houston-texans |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Bill O'Brien (American football)|Bill O'Brien]] named McKinney the backup inside linebacker behind [[Brian Cushing]] and Akeem Dent to start the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 12, 2015 |title=Texans v. Chiefs: New (Unofficial) Houston Texans Depth Chart |url=https://www.battleredblog.com/platform/amp/2015/9/12/9309281/texans-v-chiefs-new-unofficial-houston-texans-depth-chart |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=battleredblog.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Texans' season-opener against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] and recorded one solo tackle in their 27–20 loss. In Week 3, McKinney earned his first career start after head coach Bill O'Brien opted to start the rookie over Akeem Dent. He recorded four combined tackles in the Texans' 19–9 win against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. On October 18, 2015, he made his third career start and recorded three combined tackles during a 31–20 victory at the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He left the game in the third quarter after sustaining a [[concussion]] and missed the next two games (Weeks 7–8).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gurzi, Randy |date=October 24, 2015 |title=Texans vs. Dolphins injury roundup: Jackson out, Clowney questionable |url=https://www.torotimes.com/2015/10/24/texans-vs-dolphins-injury-roundup-jackson-out-clowney-questionable/ |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=torotimes.com}}</ref> In Week 14, McKinney made a season-high ten combined tackles during a 27–6 loss to the [[New England Patriots]]. The following week, he recorded seven combined tackles and made his first career sack on [[Andrew Luck]] in the Texans' 16–10 win at the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He finished his rookie season with  63 combined tackles (37 solo) and one sack in 14 games and 11 starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benardrick McKinney (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benardrickmckinney/2552490/careerstats |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

The Texans finished first in the [[AFC South]] with a 9–7 record and received a playoff berth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Houston Texans Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/htx/2015.htm |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 9, 2016, McKinney started his first career playoff game and recorded nine combined tackles as the Texans were routed 30–0 by the Kansas City Chiefs in the AFC wildcard game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Kansas City Chiefs at Houston Texans - January 9th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601090htx.htm |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2016====
McKinney was slated as the starting inside linebacker heading into the regular season along with Brian Cushing and outside linebackers [[Jadeveon Clowney]] and [[Whitney Mercilus]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2016 |title=Texans release unofficial depth chart for Chicago |url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-release-unofficial-depth-chart-for-Chicago/476cd394-412a-4103-a073-8fb6c52300ef |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180226212109/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-release-unofficial-depth-chart-for-Chicago/476cd394-412a-4103-a073-8fb6c52300ef |archive-date=February 26, 2018 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=houstontexans.com}}</ref> On September 22, 2016, McKinney recorded a career-high 16 combined tackles (ten solo) and a sack on [[Jacoby Brissett]] as the Texans were routed by the Patriots 27–0. The following week, he collected nine combined tackles and forced the first fumble of his career in a 27–20 win against the [[Tennessee Titans]]. On October 15, 2016, McKinney recorded 12 combined tackles and a sack during a 26–23 win against the Colts.<ref name="stats16">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benardrick McKinney (2016) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benardrickmckinney/2552490/gamelogs?season=2016 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> McKinney was awarded second-team [[All-Pro]] after finishing the regular season as the only inside linebacker in the NFL with at least 100 tackles and five sacks. He finished the season with a total of 129 combined tackles (79 solo), five sacks, and two pass deflections in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career" /> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave McKinney an overall grade of 81.0 in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whitfield, Brett |date=May 25, 2017 |title=Best player under 25 years old at every defensive position |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/news/pro-best-player-under-25-years-old-at-every-defensive-position |access-date=February 25, 2018}}</ref>

For the second consecutive year, the Texans finished first in their division with a 9–7 record and made it to the playoffs. On January 7, 2017, the Texans played the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the AFC wild card game and McKinney recorded seven tackles in a 27–14 victory. They were eliminated from the playoffs the following week after being defeated by the eventual [[Super Bowl LI]] Champions, the Patriots in the AFC Divisional Round.<ref name="stats16" />

====2017====
McKinney returned as the Texans' starting inside linebacker under new defensive coordinator [[Mike Vrabel]]. He started the Texans' season-opener against the Jaguars and recorded a season-high 11 combined tackles and a forced fumble during a 29–7 loss. The following week, McKinney collected six combined tackles and sacked quarterback [[Andy Dalton]] twice in the Texans' 13–9 win at the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. In Week 11, he made a season-high tying seven solo tackle and an assisted tackle as the Texans defeated the [[Arizona Cardinals]] 31–21.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Benardrick McKinney (2017) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/benardrickmckinney/2552490/gamelogs?season=2017 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> McKinney finished his third season in {{NFL Year|2017}} with 95 combined tackles (62 solo), three sacks, and a pass deflection in 16 games and 16 starts.<ref name="career" /> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave McKinney an overall grade of 79.7, which ranked him 24th among all qualifying linebackers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pro Football Focus: Benardrick McKinney |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/benardrick-mckinney/9476 |access-date=February 25, 2018 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

====2018====
On June 14, 2018, McKinney signed a five-year, $50 million contract extension with the Texans with $21 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wesseling, Chris |date=June 14, 2018 |title=Texans sign Benardrick McKinney to 5-year, $50M deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/texans-sign-benardrick-mckinney-to-5-year-50m-deal-0ap3000000937411 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2019====
In week 6 against the Chiefs, McKinney recovered a fumble by [[Patrick Mahomes]] in the 31–24 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2019 |title=Watson, Hyde lead Chiefs to 31–24 victory over Chiefs |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128119 |access-date=October 13, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

====2020====
On October 13, 2020, McKinney was placed on season-ending [[injured reserve]] with a shoulder injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2020 |title=Texans place Benardrick McKinney on IR |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-place-benardrick-mckinney-on-ir |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On March 17, 2021, McKinney and a 2021 seventh-round pick was traded to the Dolphins in exchange for defensive end [[Shaq Lawson]] and a 2021 sixth-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2021 |title=Miami Dolphins Make 2 Trades |url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/miami-dolphins-make-2-trades |website=MiamiDolphins.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon, Grant |date=March 14, 2021 |title=Texans trading Pro Bowl LB Benardrick McKinney to Dolphins for Shaq Lawson |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/texans-to-trade-pro-bowl-lb-benardrick-mckinney-to-dolphins-for-shaq-lawson |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was released before the season on August 31.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Dolphins Announce Roster Moves – August 31|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/roster-moves-dolphins-announce-roster-moves-august-31|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On October 19, 2021, McKinney was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants sign veteran LB Benardrick McKinney to practice squad|url=https://www.giants.com/news/benardrick-mckinney-practice-squad-roster-move-transactions-houston-texans|author= Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=October 19, 2021}}</ref> On October 23, McKinney was elevated from the practice to the active roster for week 7 game against the [[Carolina Panthers]]<ref>{{cite web|title=LB Benardrick McKinney, DT David Moa activated; WR David Sills signed from practice squad|url=https://www.giants.com/news/benardrick-mckinney-david-moa-activated-david-sills-signed-carolina-panthers|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=October 23, 2021}}</ref> On November 1, McKinney was elevated from the practice squad for the second time of the season for week  8 game against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=November 1, 2021 |title=Giants activate 4; LB Carter Coughlin to IR |url=https://www.giants.com/news/benardrick-mckinney-aaron-robinson-trent-harris-steven-parker-carter-coughlin |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> On November 4, McKinney was activated off the practice squad as a [[COVID-19]] replacement and reverted to the practice squad four days later.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=November 4, 2021 |title=Notebook: 3 Giants on reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.giants.com/news/las-vegas-raiders-saquon-barkley-xavier-mckinney-gary-brightwell-covid-19 |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Giants.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Giants terminate practice squad contract of RB Dexter Williams|url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2021/11/09/new-york-giants-terminate-practice-squad-contract-dexter-williams/|author=Benton, Dan|website=Giantswire.com|date=November 9, 2021}}</ref> On November 17, McKinney was signed to the active roster.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=November 17, 2021 |title=Giants add LB Benardrick McKinney to active roster |url=https://www.giants.com/news/benardrick-mckinney-roster-move-active-jonathan-williams-practice-squad |access-date=2024-10-29 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

'''Benny L. Johnson''' (June 29, 1948 – August 10, 1988) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] who played five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Houston Oilers]] and [[New Orleans Saints]]. He was selected by the Oilers in the sixth round of the [[1970 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] at [[Johnson C. Smith University]]. He also played for the [[Philadelphia Bell]] of the [[World Football League]] (WFL).

==Early life and college==
Benny L. Johnson was born on June 29, 1948, in [[Fort Valley, Georgia]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/j/john02400.html | title=Benny Johnson | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Jones High School (Orlando, Florida)|Jones High School]] in [[Orlando, Florida]].<ref name="Pfa"/>

He played [[college football]] for the [[Johnson C. Smith Golden Bulls]] of [[Johnson C. Smith University]] from 1966 to 1969.<ref name="Pfa"/>

==Professional career==
Johnson was selected by the [[Houston Oilers]] in the sixth round, with the 144th overall pick, of the [[1970 NFL draft]].<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JohnBe20.htm | title=Benny Johnson | publisher=Pro Football Reference | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He played in all 14 games for the Oilers during his rookie season in 1970, returning 15 kicks for 320 yards.<ref name="Pfr"/> He appeared in ten games, starting four, in 1971.<ref name="Pfr"/> He played in all 14 games, starting ten, during the 1972 season, totaling one interception for 34 yards, 13 kick returns for 230 yards, one fumble, and two fumble recoveries.<ref name="Pfr"/> Johnson played in 13 games, starting four, in 1973.<ref name="Pfr"/> He became a free agent after the 1973 season.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/j/john02400.html | title=Benny Johnson NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref>

Johnson signed with the [[Philadelphia Bell]] of the [[World Football League]] on July 3, 1974.<ref name="Pst">{{cite web | url=https://prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Benny+Johnson&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search | title=Search Results | publisher=prosportstransactions.com | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref> He recorded one interception for the Bell during the 1974 season.<ref name="Pfa"/>

On May 29, 1975, the Oilers traded the rights to Johnson and [[Booker Brown]] to the [[San Diego Chargers]] for [[Carl Mauck]].<ref name="Pst"/> Johnson was waived by the Chargers on September 10, 1975.<ref name="Pst"/>

He was claimed off waivers by the [[Denver Broncos]] on September 11, 1975, but was waived soon later on September 17, 1975.<ref name="Pst"/>

Johnson was signed by the [[New Orleans Saints]] on March 29, 1976.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in nine games for the Saints during the 1976 season.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was released in 1977.<ref name="transactions"/>

==Personal life==
Johnson spent time as a volunteer assistant coach at his alma mater, Jones High School.<ref name="Orl"/> On August 10, 1988, at the age of 40, he died of a heart attack while jogging in Orlando, Florida.<ref name="Pfr"/><ref name="Orl">{{cite news | url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1988/08/12/former-nfl-jones-high-star-johnson-dies-at-40/ | title=FORMER NFL, JONES HIGH STAR JOHNSON DIES AT 40 | work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] | date=August 12, 1988 | accessdate=25 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Bernard Henry''' (born April 9, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Indianapolis Colts|Baltimore/Indianapolis Colts]] and [[Los Angeles Rams]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]].

==Early life and college==
Bernard Henry was born on April 9, 1960, in [[Los Angeles, California]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/h/henr00400.html | title=BERNARD HENRY | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=16 April 2025}}</ref> He attended [[John C. Fremont High School]] in Los Angeles.<ref name="Pfa"/>

Henry was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]] of [[Arizona State University]] from 1978 to 1981.<ref name="Pfa"/> He caught six passes for 94 yards and one touchdown in 1978, 27 passes for 301 yards and one touchdown in 1979, eight passes for	75 yards in 1980, and 39	passes for 647 yards and eight touchdowns in 1981.<ref name="Sr"/> His eight receiving touchdowns in 1981 were the most in the [[Pac-10]] that season.<ref name="Sr">{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bernard-henry-1.html?__hstc=223721476.cf5f44155f2e36f92dc58b684a6e9a44.1694291523663.1744770249365.1744778410301.1323&__hssc=223721476.1.1744778410301&__hsfp=396142232 | title=Bernard Henry | publisher=[[Sports Reference]] | accessdate=16 April 2025}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1982 NFL draft]], Henry signed with the [[Baltimore Colts]] on May 5, 1982.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in six games for the Colts during the 1982 season and recorded seven receptions for 110 yards.<ref name="Pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HenrBe00.htm | title=BERNARD HENRY | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=16 April 2025}}</ref> He was released on August 29, 1983, but re-signed the next day.<ref name="transactions"/> Henry appeared in 15 games, starting seven, in 1983, catching 30 passes for 416 yards and four touchdowns.<ref name="Pfr"/> He played in 14 games for the newly renamed Indianapolis Colts in 1984 and caught 11 passes for 139 yards and two touchdowns.<ref name="Pfr"/> He started the first game of the 1985 season, catching two passes for 31 yards, before being released on September 12, 1985.<ref name="transactions"/><ref name="Pfr"/>

On September 23, 1987, Henry signed with the [[Los Angeles Rams]] during the [[1987 NFL players strike]].<ref name="transactions"/> He appeared in three games, starting two, for the Rams and made one 13-yard reception.<ref name="Pfr"/> He was released on October 19, 1987, after the strike ended.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/h/henr00400.html | title=Bernard Henry Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=16 April 2025}}</ref>

'''Bennie Fowler III''' (born June 10, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]] and was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2014.

==Early life==
Fowler attended [[Detroit Country Day School]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bennie Fowler, Detroit Country Day, Wide Receiver |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Bennie-Fowler-8234/high-school-2890/ |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rexrode |first=Joe |date=February 20, 2016 |title=Bennie Fowler enjoying post-Super Bowl life in Michigan |url=https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/college/msu/football/2016/02/20/bennie-fowler-enjoying-post-super-bowl-life-michigan/80628220/ |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=Lansing State Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> where he was named to SuperPrep and [[PrepStar]]'s All-Midwest Teams. He was also listed among the Midwest's top prospects by SuperPrep at No. 72, he was also rated among the nations top wide receivers by Scouts, Inc. at No. 80. He was also ranked among the state's top seniors by the ''[[Lansing State Journal]]'' at No. 15 overall, [[Rivals.com]] at No. 15 also, ''[[The Detroit News]]'' at No. 16, and the ''[[Detroit Free Press]]'' at No. 16. He was also named to the ''Detroit Free Press'' All-State Division 4 Team. He was also named All-State honorable mention as an all-purpose player by the [[Associated Press]]. He was also selected to the All-County Dream Team by ''[[The Oakland Press]]'' and All-North Team by ''The Detroit News''.<ref name="msu" />

As a [[Eleventh grade|junior]] in 2007, Fowler missed five games during the season with a broken [[collarbone]]. For the season, he recorded 12 receptions for 265 yards and four touchdowns. As a [[Twelfth grade|senior]] in 2008, he accounted for a total of 1,478 all-purpose yards and 15 touchdowns. He recorded 32 receptions for 683 yards and six touchdowns. On defense, he recorded 16 tackles, three sacks, and three pass-break ups while returning five punts for 218 yards and five kickoffs for 122 yards.<ref name="msu" />

In his [[high school football|high school]] career, Fowler recorded 44 receptions for 903 yards and 10 touchdowns, he also [[Rush (gridiron football)#Offense|rushed]] the ball 58 times for 542 yards and nine touchdowns.<ref name="msu" />

In addition to playing football, Fowler won the [[Oakland County, Michigan|Oakland County]] 100-meter and state long jump titles in 2008. He was also a member of the Detroit Country Day School Yellow Jackets' 2007 state championship basketball team.<ref name="msu" />

==College career==
After graduating from high school, Fowler attended [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bennie Fowler College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bennie-fowler-1.html |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=June 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624222634/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/bennie-fowler-1.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

As a [[Freshman#United States|freshman]] in [[2009 Michigan State Spartans football team|2009]], Fowler [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] with a [[stress fracture]] in his foot.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leung |first=Diamond |date=November 26, 2013 |title=Michigan State receiver Bennie Fowler has option to petition for sixth year of eligibility |url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2013/11/michigan_state_receiver_bennie_4.html |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=mlive.com |language=en |archive-date=May 22, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220522211956/https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2013/11/michigan_state_receiver_bennie_4.html |url-status=live }}</ref> As a redshirt freshman, in [[2010 Michigan State Spartans football team|2010]], he appeared in all 13 games and finished sixth on the team with 573 all-purpose yards. He recorded 14 receptions for 175 yards, and carried the ball seven times for 62 yards. He also returned 15 kickoffs for 336 yards. His return yards ranked second on the team behind [[Keshawn Martin]]. Fowler also recorded a career best 161 all-purpose yards against No. 15 [[2010 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama]] in the [[2011 Capital One Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Capital One Bowl - Michigan State vs Alabama Box Score, January 1, 2011 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-01-01-alabama.html |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=August 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814023448/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-01-01-alabama.html |url-status=live }}</ref> As a redshirt [[Sophomore#Post-secondary education|sophomore]] in [[2011 Michigan State Spartans football team|2011]], he appeared in just five games due to a foot injury. He recorded two receptions for 20 yards and one carry for six yards. As a redshirt [[Junior (education year)#College|junior]] in [[2012 Michigan State Spartans football team|2012]], he led the team with 524 receiving yards and four touchdowns and ranked second with 41 receptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 Michigan State Spartans Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/michigan-state/2012.html |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=June 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220628151548/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/michigan-state/2012.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He also tied for the lead the team with seven receptions of 20-plus yards. As a redshirt [[Senior (education)#Intercollegiate athletics|senior]] in [[2013 Michigan State Spartans football team|2013]], he again led the team in receiving yards, with 622 yards, and touchdowns, with six.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 Michigan State Spartans Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/michigan-state/2013.html |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230130204553/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/michigan-state/2013.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He also ranked third on the team with 36 receptions. He finished second on the team with 10 receptions for 20-plus yards. Fowler's six touchdowns ranked sixth in the [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] in 2013.<ref name="msu" />

===Denver Broncos===
====2014 season====
On May 10, 2014, the [[Denver Broncos]] signed Fowler as an undrafted free agent to a one-year, $114,000 contract.<ref name="earnings">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Bennie Fowler earnings |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/denver-broncos/bennie-fowler-14864/cash-earnings/ |access-date=March 10, 2018 |website=spotrac.com |archive-date=March 20, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180320024512/http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/denver-broncos/bennie-fowler-14864/cash-earnings/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=2014-05-11 |title=Broncos announce 15-man rookie free agent class |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/broncos-announce-15-man-rookie-free-agent-class |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190206010506/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/05/11/broncos-announce-15-man-rookie-free-agent-class/ |archive-date=February 6, 2019 |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> On August 30, 2014, he was [[Waivers (American football)|waived]] by the Broncos as part of their final roster cuts. On August 31, 2014, he was signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Griffith |first=Mike |date=April 16, 2016 |title=Bennie Fowler signs deal to return to Super Bowl champion Denver Broncos |url=http://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2016/04/bennie_fowler_signs_deal_to_re.html |access-date=August 29, 2016 |website=MLive.com |archive-date=June 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624010620/https://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2016/04/bennie_fowler_signs_deal_to_re.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Darymond">{{Cite web |last=Legwold |first=Jeff |date=October 16, 2015 |title=Bennie Fowler makes most of chances to carve out role |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/183975/bennie-fowler-makes-most-of-chances-to-carve-out-role |access-date=August 29, 2016 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=September 11, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911140741/http://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/183975/bennie-fowler-makes-most-of-chances-to-carve-out-role |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2015 season====
[[Image:BennieFowlerBroncos.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Fowler with the Broncos in 2015]]
On January 15, 2015, the Denver Broncos signed Fowler to a one-year, $550,000 reserve/future contract.<ref name="earnings" />

Fowler played in all 16 regular season games for the Broncos, ending the [[2015 Denver Broncos season|2015 season]] with 16 receptions for 203 yards. On February 7, 2016, Fowler was part of the Broncos team that defeated the [[2015 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] by a score of 24–10 in [[Super Bowl 50]]. Towards the end of the game, Fowler caught a pass for a two-point conversion from quarterback [[Peyton Manning]] to make it a 14-point game and cement the Broncos' third Super Bowl title.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=February 7, 2016 |title=Broncos outlast Panthers, claim third Super Bowl title |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/broncos-outlast-panthers-claim-third-super-bowl-title-0ap3000000634371 |access-date=August 7, 2017 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=February 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227065512/https://www.nfl.com/news/broncos-outlast-panthers-claim-third-super-bowl-title-0ap3000000634371 |url-status=live }}</ref> Notably, this would be the final pass of Manning's career.
<!-- Please do not add anything about the two-point conversion from the Super Bowl. It's been removed numerous times for being pure trivia. The information was brought up on the NFL project talk page in spring 2016. -->

On April 15, 2016, Fowler re-signed with the Broncos.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolfe |first=Cameron |date=April 15, 2016 |title=Bennie Fowler, Sam Brenner sign tenders to return to Broncos for 2016 season |url=http://www.denverpost.com/2016/04/15/bennie-fowler-sam-brenner-sign-tenders-to-return-to-broncos-for-2016-season/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160914075401/http://www.denverpost.com/2016/04/15/bennie-fowler-sam-brenner-sign-tenders-to-return-to-broncos-for-2016-season/ |archive-date=September 14, 2016 |access-date=August 29, 2016 |website=Denver Post}}</ref>

====2016 season====
Fowler appeared in 13 games and recorded 11 receptions for 145 yards and two touchdowns in the 2016 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bennie Fowler 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FowlBe00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126003024/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FowlBe00/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2017 season====

==Personal life==
Bennie Fowler is the son of Bennie Fowler Jr. and Teresa Gueyser.<ref name="msu">{{Cite web |title=Bennie Fowler – Football |url=https://msuspartans.com/sports/football/roster/bennie-fowler/1952 |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=Michigan State University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He has a younger brother, Chris Fowler, who played basketball at Central Michigan University.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Snyder |first=Mark |date=March 12, 2015 |title=Dad helped develop CMU's Chris Fowler into a leader |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2015/03/12/chris-fowler-central-michigan/70243472/ |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=Detroit Free Press |language=en-US |archive-date=March 15, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315233719/http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/2015/03/12/chris-fowler-central-michigan/70243472/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He also has a younger sister who played volleyball at Florida Southern.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Madison Fowler – 2023 – Women's Volleyball |url=https://fscmocs.com/sports/womens-volleyball/roster/madison-fowler/5113 |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=Florida Southern College |language=en}}</ref> He is also longtime friends with [[Golden State Warriors]] [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] [[Draymond Green]], who also attended Michigan State.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Swanson |first=Ben |date=October 11, 2015 |title=As Fowler grows, close friend and NBA champion Draymond Green hopes to see similar path |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/as-fowler-grows-close-friend-and-nba-champion-draymond-green-hopes-to-s-16056708 |access-date=May 22, 2023 |website=DenverBroncos.com |language=en-US |archive-date=June 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625110736/https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/as-fowler-grows-close-friend-and-nba-champion-draymond-green-hopes-to-s-16056708 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On April 10, 2025, it was announced that Fowler would be joining the DNVR Broncos podcast following the departure of previous host [[Todd Davis (American football)|Todd Davis]] to join the Broncos' coaching staff.

'''Benjamin Snell Jr.''' (born February 26, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky Wildcats]]. Snell's paternal grandfather was a first cousin of former [[New York Jets]] running back [[Matt Snell]].  His father, Benjamin Snell Sr. is an alumnus of [[Ohio Northern University]], played in the [[NFL]] and the [[XFL (2001)|XFL]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenawalt |first=Tyler |date=March 1, 2019 |title=Kentucky's Benny Snell Jr. wants to follow in great uncle's footsteps with Jets |url=https://jetswire.usatoday.com/2019/03/01/kentucky-benny-snell-jr-matt-snell-jets/ |access-date=December 8, 2019 |website=Jets Wire |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Snell Jr. attended [[Westerville Central High School]].<ref name="wapost_27sept18" /> During his time there, he won two Ohio Capital Conference titles. During his junior season, Snell Jr. rushed for 2,077 yards while scoring 26 [[touchdowns]] on the ground, he also had two receiving touchdowns that year. As a senior, he totaled 1,826 rushing yards, 264 receiving yards and 29 touchdowns. Snell Jr. was rated as a three-star recruit.<ref name="wapost_27sept18">{{Cite web |last=Giambalvo |first=Emily  |date=September 27, 2018 |title=Benny Snell Jr. will make you believe in Kentucky football |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/amphtml/sports/2018/09/27/benny-snell-jr-will-make-you-believe-kentucky-football/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180928154727/https://www.washingtonpost.com/amphtml/sports/2018/09/27/benny-snell-jr-will-make-you-believe-kentucky-football/ |archive-date=2018-09-28 |website=Washington Post}}</ref> He chose [[Kentucky Wildcats football|Kentucky]] over [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]], [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati]], [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College]], [[Toledo Rockets football|Toledo]] and [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia]].

==College career==
[[File:Benny Snell, Jr.jpg|thumb|left|Snell with Kentucky in 2018]]

===Freshman===
As a freshman in [[2016 Kentucky Wildcats football team|2016]], Snell rushed for 1,091 yards, breaking the Kentucky freshman rushing record which was held by [[Moe Williams]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2018 |title=KSR Timeline: Benny Snell's Rise to Fame |url=https://kentuckysportsradio.com/football-2/ksr-timeline-benny-snells-rise-to-fame/ |access-date=September 18, 2020 |website=Kentucky Sports Radio |language=en-US}}</ref> Snell Jr. managed to score 13 rushing touchdowns. During his freshman season, Snell Jr set six Kentucky freshman records, including most rushing touchdowns in a game (4), most rushing yards by a freshman (1,091), most rushing touchdowns by a freshman (13), most total touchdowns by a freshman (13), most 100-yard rushing games (5) and most rushing yards by a freshman in a single game (192). At the end of his freshman season Snell Jr, was selected as a True Freshman [[All-American]] by [[ESPN]] and [[247Sports]], [[Football Writers Association of America]] (FWAA) Freshman All-American, Freshman All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) and a Second-team All-SEC pick by [[Pro Football Focus]].

===Sophomore===
As a sophomore in [[2017 Kentucky Wildcats football team|2017]], Snell rushed for 1,333 rushing yards and scored 19 rushing touchdowns. Snell Jr. became the first Kentucky player with 10 or more career 100-yard rushing games prior to his junior season. He became the only SEC player since 2000 to have at least 116 rushing yards and at least three rushing touchdowns in three consecutive games. Snell Jr. became the ninth player in school history to reach 2,000 rushing yards in his career and the 19th player in SEC history to reach 2,000 career rushing yards prior to his junior season. He became the only player in school history to have back-to-back 1,000 rushing yard seasons. Snell Jr. was selected as a preseason Associated Press All-SEC First-team<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2018 |title=Tennessee's Trey Smith Named to Coaches Preseason All-SEC First Team |url=https://www.chattanoogan.com/2018/8/23/374982/Tennessee-s-Trey-Smith-Named-to-Coaches.aspx |access-date=May 24, 2026 |website=Chattanoogan.com}}</ref> and All-SEC Second-team. In addition, Snell Jr. was put on the [[Doak Walker Award|Doak Walker Award Watch List]] and the [[Maxwell Award|Maxwell Award Watch List]].

===Junior===
As a junior in [[2018 Kentucky Wildcats football team|2018]], Snell rushed for 1,449 rushing yards and scored 16 rushing touchdowns. Snell Jr. became one of four running backs in SEC history to have three consecutive 1,000 rushing yard seasons, the others being [[Herschel Walker]], [[Darren McFadden]], and [[Alex Collins (American football)|Alex Collins]]. Snell Jr. would also become the school's career rushing yards leader after scoring on a 12-yard touchdown run against the  [[2018 Penn State Nittany Lions football team|Penn State Nittany Lions]] in the [[2019 Citrus Bowl]]. This 43-year-old record, previously held by [[Sonny Collins]], was broken in just three seasons by Snell.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terry |first=Derek |date=January 1, 2019 |title=Benny Snell becomes Kentucky's all-time leading rusher |url=https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Article/Kentucky-football-Benny-Snell-rushing-record-127160258/ |access-date=September 18, 2020 |website=CatsPause|via=247sports}}</ref> Snell was voted First-team All-SEC by SEC Coaches.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 All-SEC Football Team announced |url=http://www.secsports.com/article/25450830/2018-all-sec-football-team-announced |access-date=September 18, 2020 |website=www.secsports.com}}</ref> He would announce on December 14, 2018, that he would forgo his senior season and enter the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hale |first=John |date=December 14, 2018 |title=Benny Snell headed to NFL draft but will play for UK in Citrus Bowl |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2018/12/14/kentucky-football-benny-snell-declares-nfl-draft/2314215002/ |access-date=September 18, 2020 |website=The Courier-Journal}}</ref>

Snell was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the fourth round with the 122nd overall pick in the 2019 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 27, 2019 |title=Steelers select Snell Jr. in fourth round |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-select-snell-jr-in-fourth-round |website=Steelers.com}}</ref>

In Week 13 against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Snell rushed 16 times for 63 yards and his first career rushing touchdown in the 20–13 win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 1, 2019 |title=Duck's Dynasty? Backup Hodges leads Steelers by Browns 20-13 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128107 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191202101856/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128107 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 2, 2019 |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In Week 17 against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Snell rushed 18 times for 91 yards and a touchdown during the 28–10 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 29, 2019 |title=Despite lacking star power, Ravens beat Steelers 28-10 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127950 |access-date=December 29, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> As a rookie, Snell finished with 108 carries for 426 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Snell 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SnelBe00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 7, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Snell's first big breakthrough came on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' against the [[New York Giants]] in Week 1 of the 2020 season after starter [[James Conner (American football)|James Conner]] suffered an injury. He finished with 19 carries for 113 rushing yards as the Steelers won 26–16.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at New York Giants - September 14th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009140nyg.htm |access-date=September 18, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>
In Week 15 against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on ''Monday Night Football'', Snell recorded 107 yards from scrimmage and a rushing touchdown during the 27–17 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals - December 21st, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012210cin.htm |access-date=2020-12-21 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Jones re-signed with the Dolphins on March 20, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dolphins Re-sign Jones|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-re-sign-jones|website=MiamiDolphins.com|date=March 20, 2025}}</ref> He played in 14 games (including eight starts), recording 15 tackles, one sack, and a pass deflection. On December 27, Jones was placed on season-ending injured reserve due to a back injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dolphins Make Roster Moves|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-make-roster-moves-x4787|access-date=January 21, 2026|website=miamidolphins.com|language=en}}</ref>

'''Benjamin St-Juste''' ({{IPAc-en|s|eɪ|n|t|ˈ|dʒ|uː|s|t}} {{respell|saint|JOOST}};<ref>{{cite AV media|title=Juiced up! Ben St-Juste on transitioning to the NFL|via=YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B0tnBvZyAfQ|time=7:46|date=October 30, 2021|access-date=September 5, 2022|website=YouTube}}</ref> born September 8, 1997) is a Canadian professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). A native of [[Montreal]], he played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] and [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]] prior to being selected by [[Washington Football Team]] in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
St-Juste was born on September 8, 1997, in [[Montreal]], [[Canada]], to a [[Haitians|Haitian]] father and [[French-Canadian]] mother.<ref name="FrenchHaitian">{{cite web |last1=Greder |first1=Andy |title=Benjamin St-Juste takes winding road: Montreal to Michigan to Gophers |url=https://www.twincities.com/2019/10/10/benjamin-st-juste-takes-winding-road-from-montreal-to-michigan-to-gophers/ |website=TwinCities.com |date=10 October 2019 |publisher=[[Pioneer Press]] |access-date=9 May 2021}}</ref> He grew up speaking [[French language|French]] and [[Haitian Creole]] before learning [[English language|English]] at [[Cégep du Vieux Montréal]].<ref name="School">{{cite news |last1=Kryk |first1=John |title=Kryk's Canadian NFL Draft profile: Benjamin St-Juste of Montreal |url=https://torontosun.com/sports/football/nfl/kryks-canadian-nfl-draft-profile-benjamin-st-juste-of-montreal|date=April 27, 2021|newspaper=Toronto Sun}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Ryan |first1=Megan|url=https://www.startribune.com/gophers-land-a-hidden-canadian-gem-in-michigan-transfer-benjamin-st-juste/562875762/|title=Gophers land a hidden Canadian gem in Michigan transfer Benjamin St-Juste|date=October 11, 2019|website=[[Star Tribune]]}}</ref> St-Juste played [[ice hockey]] as a youth, later taking an interest in [[American football]] because of his father Wilbert, who was a member of the [[1989 Miami Hurricanes football team]] but broke his leg in preseason camp.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greder |first1=Andy |title=With NFL next, Gophers' Benjamin St-Juste tries to pave way for other Canadians |url=https://www.bemidjipioneer.com/sports/football/7003653-With-NFL-next-Gophers%E2%80%99-Benjamin-St-Juste-tries-to-pave-way-for-other-Canadians |website=bemidjipioneer.com |date=27 April 2021 |publisher=[[St. Paul Pioneer Press]] |access-date=13 May 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
St-Juste attended various [[college football]] camps in the United States in the mid-2010s, and was offered a scholarship to play for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] under [[Jim Harbaugh]].<ref name="School"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2016/05/benjamin_st-juste_goes_from_un.html|first=Matt|last=Wenzel|title=Benjamin St-Juste goes from unknown Canadian commodity to Michigan commit|date=May 12, 2016|website=MLive}}</ref> He played in 12 games for the Wolverines as a freshman in 2017, but [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]ed as a sophomore the following year due to a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hartman |first=Sid |date=November 21, 2019 |title=French Canadian Benjamin St.-Juste followed a unique path to starting for ===Washington Football Team / Commanders===
St-Juste was selected by the [[Washington Football Team]] in the third round (74th overall) of the [[2021 NFL draft]], in which they took St-Juste with one of the two picks they acquired in a trade that sent [[Trent Williams]] to the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Washington Football Team Picks Minnesota CB Benjamin St. Juste - NFL Draft |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/washingtonfootball/news/washington-football-team-picks-minnesota-cb-benjamin-st-juste-nfl-draft |website=SI.com |access-date=3 May 2021|first=Grant|last=Afseth}}</ref> He was also selected by the [[Toronto Argonauts]] in the sixth round (52nd overall) of the [[2021 CFL draft]] shortly after.<ref>{{cite news |title=Argos welcome 2021 CFL Draft class |url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2021/05/04/argos-welcome-2021-cfl-draft-class/ |website=Argonauts.ca |date=May 4, 2021 |access-date=May 5, 2021}}</ref> St-Juste signed his four-year rookie contract with Washington on May 13, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stackpole |first1=Kyle |title=Washington Signs 2021 Draft Class |url=https://www.washingtonfootball.com/news/washington-2021-draft-class-signs-contracts |website=WashingtonFootball.com |access-date=May 13, 2021 |date=May 13, 2021}}</ref> He made his NFL debut in the opening game against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], where he recorded four tackles, but also allowed six catches in a 20–16 loss.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greder |first1=Andy |title=Gophers in the NFL: Ben St-Juste endures tough debut; Ryan Santoso makes first points |url=https://www.twincities.com/2021/09/13/gophers-in-the-nfl-ben-st-juste-endures-tough-debut-ryan-santoso-makes-first-points/ |website=TwinCities.com |publisher=Pioneer Press |access-date=15 September 2021 |date=13 September 2021}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] in December 2021 due to lingering issues from a concussion.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Trotta |first1=Jerry |title=Here's why Benjamin St-Juste landing on IR isn't a significant loss |url=https://riggosrag.com/2021/12/05/why-benjamin-st-juste-landing-ir-isnt-significant/ |website=RiggosRag.com |date=5 December 2021 |access-date=7 March 2022}}</ref>

St-Juste moved from outside corner to the slot for the 2022 season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Morales |first1=PJ |title=Commanders CB Benjamin St-Juste slides to slot for Year 2 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/07/19/benjamin-st-juste-commanders-slot/\ |newspaper=The Washington Post |access-date=19 July 2022}}</ref> He was moved back to outside corner following the benching of [[William Jackson III]] in Week 5.<ref>{{cite web|work=Commmanders.com|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-trust-steadily-improving-st-juste-with-toughest-assignments|title=Commanders trust steadily improving St-Juste with toughest assignments|date=November 11, 2022|accessdate=November 11, 2022|first=Matthew|last=Paras}}</ref> With 35 seconds remaining and the [[Chicago Bears]] on fourth and goal, St-Juste made a key stop pushing wide receiver [[Darnell Mooney]], who caught the pass, out of the endzone before Mooney's feet landed on the field and sealed the Commanders' 12-7 victory.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/10/14/commanders-bears-defense-st-juste/|title=Inside the defensive stand that sealed the Commanders' win over the Bears|first=Sam|last=Fortier|date=October 14, 2022|accessdate=December 5, 2022}}</ref> In Week 9 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], he deflected a touchdown pass attempt from [[Kirk Cousins]] which cornerback [[Danny Johnson (American football)|Danny Johnson]] intercepted.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-fail-to-overcome-mistakes-in-20-17-loss-to-vikings|title=Instant Analysis Commanders fail to overcome mistakes in 20-17 loss to Vikings|date=November 6, 2022|accessdate=November 19, 2022|first=Zach|last=Selby}}</ref> The following week's victory over the then-undefeated [[Philadelphia Eagles]], St-Juste forced wide receiver [[Quez Watkins]], after catching a 50-yard pass, to fumble the ball allowing safety [[Darrick Forrest]] to recover it.<ref>{{cite web|work=Commanders.com|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/5-takeaways-from-the-commanders-eagles-upset-win-on-monday-night-football|title=5 takeaways from the Commanders' upset win on Monday Night Football|date=November 15, 2022|first=Zach|last=Selby|accessdate=November 16, 2022}}</ref> On January 6, 2023, he was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web|work=Commanders.com|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-place-saahdiq-charles-benjamin-st-juste-on-ir|title=Commanders place Saahdiq Charles, Benjamin St-Juste on IR|date=January 6, 2023|accessdate=January 7, 2023|first=Zach|last=Selby}}</ref>

He played in all 17 regular season games (with 14 starts) and recorded 71 tackles, seven pass deflections, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-2024-position-review-cornerback|work=Commanders.com|title=Commanders 2024 position review {{!}} Cornerback|date=February 4, 2025|accessdate=July 25, 2025|first=Zach|last=Selby}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On March 12, 2025, St-Juste signed a one-year contract with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/agree-to-terms-with-benjamin-st-juste-2025|title=  Los Angeles Chargers Agree to Terms with Benjamin St-Juste  |work=Los Angeles Chargers|date=March 12, 2025}}</ref>

On October 12, 2025, Benjamin recorded his [https://www.chargers.com/video/benjamin-st-juste-highlight-interception-vs-dolphins-week-6-2025 first interception as a Charger] in a 29–27 win against the Miami Dolphins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Benjamin St-Juste's First Interception as a Charger Comes vs. Tua Tagovailoa |url=https://www.chargers.com/video/benjamin-st-juste-highlight-interception-vs-dolphins-week-6-2025 |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=www.chargers.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Benjamin St-Juste appeared in 16 games for the Los Angeles Chargers in 2025, making two starts while recording seven pass deflections and one interception.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Sportsnet |date=2026-03-10 |title=Report: Packers sign Canadian cornerback Benjamin St-Juste |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nfl/article/report-packers-sign-canadian-cornerback-benjamin-st-juste/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=Sportsnet.ca |language=en}}</ref>

According to Pro Football Focus (PFF), he finished the season as the NFL’s highest-graded cornerback in zone coverage (90.1), while also posting strong marks in overall coverage (77.1) and total defense (76.3). He missed just one tackle all year and contributed heavily on special teams with a career-high 296 snaps, capping off an impressive and efficient campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Jordan J. |date=2026-03-10 |title=Packers Strike $10 Million Deal With Ex-Chargers Veteran Cornerback |url=https://heavy.com/sports/nfl/green-bay-packers/benjamin-st-juste-signing-free-agency/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=HEAVY |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On March 12, 2026, St-Juste signed a two-year, $10 million contract with the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign CB Benjamin St-Juste|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-cb-benjamin-st-juste-march-12-2026|website=Packers.com|date=March 12, 2026}}</ref>

'''Benton Whitley''' (born February 12, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Cleveland Browns]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Holy Cross Crusaders football|Holy Cross Crusaders]].

==College career==
Whitley played for the [[Holy Cross Crusaders football|Holy Cross Crusaders]] for five seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/patriots/news/local-prospect-spotlight-benton-whitley-de-holy-cross|title=Local Prospect Spotlight: Benton Whitley, DE, Holy Cross|first=Kevin|last=Tame, Jr.|website=[[SI.com]]|date=March 8, 2022|access-date=September 30, 2022}}</ref> He became a starter as a junior and used the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes in 2020 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and returned to Holy Cross for a fifth season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Toland |first=Jennifer |date=August 18, 2021 |title=Holy Cross defensive lineman Benton Whitley pro-level power, ability college football Springfield |url=https://www.telegram.com/story/sports/college/2021/08/18/holy-cross-defensive-lineman-benton-whitley-pro-level-power-ability-college-football-springfield/8148633002/ |access-date=September 30, 2022 |website=[[Telegram & Gazette]]}}</ref> Whitley finished his college career with 111 tackles, 26.5 tackles for loss, and 15.5 sacks in 42 games played.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/2022/09/21/kansas-city-chiefs-benton-whitley-signed-los-angeles-rams-practice-squad/|title=Chiefs to sign DE Benton Whitley from Rams practice squad
|first=Charles|last=Goldman|website=Chiefs Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=September 21, 2022|access-date=September 30, 2022}}</ref>

'''Benjamin James Morrison''' (born March 11, 2004) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] and was selected by the Buccaneers in the second round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Morrison attended [[Brophy College Preparatory]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]]. As a senior, he had 53 tackles and two [[interceptions]]. He played in the 2022 Polynesian Bowl. Morrison committed to the [[University of Notre Dame]] to play college football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |date=July 15, 2021 |title=Brophy Prep cornerback Benjamin Morrison commits to Notre Dame Fighting Irish |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2021/07/15/brophy-prep-cb-benjamin-morris-commits-notre-dame-fighting-irish/7979050002/ |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=The Arizona Republic}}</ref>

==College career==
===2022 season===
Morrison earned immediate playing time in his true freshman year at [[2022 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|Notre Dame]] in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McKenna |first=Greg |date=September 8, 2022 |title=Where'd this guy come from? Notre Dame frosh Benjamin Morrison leaves big first impression |url=https://www.ndinsider.com/story/sports/football/2022/09/08/notre-dame-freshman-benjamin-morrison-leaves-big-first-impression-college-football-south-bend/65742616007/ |access-date=May 24, 2026 |website=Notre Dame Insider}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndinsider.com/story/sports/football/2022/10/14/notre-dame-cornerback-benjamin-morrison/69553537007/|title=How Benjamin Morrison embraced his starting cornerback role at Notre Dame|website=Notre Dame Insider}}</ref> He made his collegiate debut on September 3, 2022, against [[2022 Ohio State Buckeyes football team|Ohio State]], collecting three total tackles and a pass deflection.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Scanlon Jr. |first1=Michael |title=Notre Dame football: What surprised us against Ohio State |url=https://slapthesign.com/2022/09/06/notre-dame-football-surprised-ohio-state/ |website=slapthesign.com}}</ref> Against [[2022 California Golden Bears football team|California]] on September 17, Morrison made his first career start by tallying three tackles. He had his first two career interceptions in an upset victory over [[2022 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson]] on November 5.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/notredame/football/notre-dame-football-benjamin-morrison-shines-in-win-over-clemson-stires|title=Benjamin Morrison Shines In Notre Dame Win Over Clemson|first=Sean|last=Stires|work=Notre Dame Fighting Irish on SI |publisher=SI.com}}</ref> Two weeks later, on November 19, he had three interceptions against [[2022 Boston College Eagles football team|Boston College]], tying the NCAA single-game record.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nwitimes.com/sports/football/college/university-of-notre-dame/benjamin-morrison-grabs-3-interceptions-no-18-notre-dame-blanks-bc/article_8964e18f-3ec4-5973-89c0-d92fa67e8c97.html|title=Benjamin Morrison grabs 3 interceptions, No. 18 Notre Dame blanks BC|author=TOM COYNE|agency=Associated Press|website=nwitimes.com|access-date=November 20, 2022|archive-date=November 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221120211759/https://www.nwitimes.com/sports/football/college/university-of-notre-dame/benjamin-morrison-grabs-3-interceptions-no-18-notre-dame-blanks-bc/article_8964e18f-3ec4-5973-89c0-d92fa67e8c97.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the [[2022 Gator Bowl]], Morrison added his team-high sixth interception of the season against [[2022 South Carolina Gamecocks football team|South Carolina]].

Morrison finished the season with 33 tackles (22 of them solo), four pass breakups, six interceptions, and a pick-six. He was named Freshman All-American by [[On3.com]], [[College Football News]], [[Pro Football Focus]]. He was also named True Freshman All-American by [[The Athletic]], [[247Sports]], [[ESPN]], and by the [[Football Writers Association of America]] (FWAA).

===2023 season===
Morrison was named a preseason [[All-American]] by [[NBCSports]], FWAA, and ESPN.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Farmer |first1=Douglas |title=Notre Dame 99-to-0: No. 20 Benjamin Morrison, sophomore cornerback, preseason All-American |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/college-football/news/notre-dame-99-to-0-no-20-benjamin-morrison-sophomore-cornerback-preseason-all-american |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref> On June 9, 2023, Morrison was named the fourth best cornerback in college football.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Driskell |first1=Bryan |title=Benjamin Morrison Named College Football's No. 4 Cornerback For 2023 |url=https://www.si.com/college/notredame/football/notre-dame-football-benjamin-morrison-named-college-football-no-4-cornerback |website=FN.com |access-date=16 September 2023}}</ref> He was also placed on the watchlist for the [[Bronko Nagurski Trophy]],<ref>{{cite web |title=J.D. Bertrand and Benjamin Morrison Named to Nagurski Trophy Watch List |url=https://fightingirish.com/j-d-bertrand-and-benjamin-morrison-named-to-nagurski-trophy-watch-list/ |website=fightingirish.com |publisher=Notre Dame}}</ref> the [[Jim Thorpe Award]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Benjamin Morrison Earns Thorpe Award Watch List Selection |url=https://fightingirish.com/benjamin-morrison-earns-thorpe-award-watch-list-selection/ |website=fightingirish.com |publisher=Notre Dame}}</ref> and the [[Chuck Bednarik Award]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Benjamin Morrison Selected For Bednarik Award Watch List |url=https://fightingirish.com/benjamin-morrison-selected-for-bednarik-award-watch-list/ |website=fightingirish.com |publisher=Notre Dame}}</ref> On September 19 against [[2023 NC State Wolfpack football team|NC State]], Morrison caught his first interception of the season. He also added three solo tackles in a 45–24 victory.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Driskell |first1=Jeff |title=Game Observations - Defense: Notre Dame D Handles NC State |url=https://www.si.com/college/notredame/football/notre-dame-football-game-observations-defense-handles-nc-state |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=24 September 2023}}</ref> In a game against No. 10 [[2023 USC Trojans football team|USC]], Morrison intercepted [[Caleb Williams]], setting up [[Audric Estime|Audric Estimé]] for a one-yard touchdown run. The [[2023 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|Fighting Irish]] would end up upsetting Williams and the Trojans, 48–20.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rallo |first1=Curt |title=No. 21 Notre Dame harasses Caleb Williams and hands No. 10 USC first loss in 48-20 drubbing |url=https://www.wsls.com/sports/2023/10/15/no-21-notre-dame-harasses-caleb-williams-and-hands-no-10-usc-first-loss-in-48-20-drubbing/ |website=WSLS |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=16 October 2023}}</ref> Morrison would then be ruled out of Notre Dame's game against [[2023 Pittsburgh Panthers football team|Pittsburgh]] due to a quad injury.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Berardino |first1=Mike |title=Benjamin Morrison (quadriceps) ruled out for Notre Dame football vs. Pittsburgh |url=https://www.southbendtribune.com/story/sports/college/football/2023/10/28/notre-dame-football-loses-cornerback-benjamin-morrison-to-quad-injury-pittsburgh-jaden-mickey/71331351007/ |website=South Bend Tribune |access-date=2 November 2023}}</ref> On November 1, Morrison was named a semifinalist for the Jim Thorpe Award.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Loy |first1=Tom |title=Notre Dame CB Benjamin Morrison a Thorpe Award Semifinalist |url=https://247sports.com/college/notre-dame/article/notre-dame-cb-benjamin-morrison-a-thorpe-award-semifinalist-219305776/ |website=Irish Illustrated |access-date=2 November 2023}}</ref>

=== 2024 season ===
Morrison was once again named a preseason first team All-American by ESPN and The Sporting News.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-14 |title=Morrison Named to ESPN Preseason All-America First Team |url=https://fightingirish.com/morrison-named-to-espn-preseason-all-america-first-team/ |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=Notre Dame Fighting Irish - Official Athletics Website |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-14 |title=Cross III, Morrison, Watts Named Preseason First Team All-Americans by Sporting News |url=https://fightingirish.com/cross-iii-morrison-watts-named-preseason-first-team-all-americans-by-sporting-news/ |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=Notre Dame Fighting Irish - Official Athletics Website |language=en-US}}</ref> He totaled 20 tackles and four pass breakups in [[2024 Notre Dame Fighting Irish football team|Notre Dame]]'s first six games, including five tackles and two pass breakups in a win against [[2024 Louisville Cardinals football team|Louisville]]. Morrison's season was cut short by an injury to his hip sustained in the Irish's 49-7 win over [[2024 Stanford Cardinal football team|Stanford]], which required season-ending surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-14 |title=Notre Dame loses CB Morrison (hip) for season |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/41792988/notre-dame-loses-cb-benjamin-morrison-hip-season |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He entered the [[2025 NFL draft]] after Notre Dame's run to the [[2025 College Football Playoff National Championship|CFP National Championship Game]], where they lost to [[2024 Ohio State Buckeyes football team|Ohio State]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-01-23 |title=Notre Dame CB Benjamin Morrison ends chapter, enters NFL draft |url=https://abc7chicago.com/post/notre-dame-cb-benjamin-morrison-ends-chapter-enters-nfl-draft/15830147/ |access-date=2025-01-23 |website=ABC7 Chicago |language=en}}</ref>
