[[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]] (2021–2022) | undraftedyear = 2023 | pastteams = * [[Philadelphia Eagles]] ({{NFL Year|2023|2025}}) * [[Buffalo Bills]] ({{NFL Year|2026}}–present) | status = Active | highlights = * [[List of Super Bowl champions|Super Bowl champion]] ([[Super Bowl LIX|LIX]]) | statseason = 2024 | statweek = | statlabel1 = [[Tackle (football move)|Total tackles]] | statvalue1 = 16 | statlabel2 = [[Reception (gridiron football)|Receptions]] | statvalue2 = 1 | pfr = VanSBe00 }} '''Ben VanSumeren''' (born May 5, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] for the [[Buffalo Bills]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).{{cite news |title= Bills sign athletic fullback Ben VanSumeren to one-year deal|url=https://www.buffalobills.com/news/bills-sign-athletic-fullback-ben-vansumeren-to-one-year-deal |accessdate=April 29, 2026 |work=[[Buffalo Bills]] |date=April 29, 2026}} He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] and [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]]. VanSumeren began his NFL career as a linebacker and was officially designated as a linebacker for his first two seasons, although he only saw playing time on defense during his rookie season. After the Eagles began playing him at fullback in his second season VanSumeren officially moved to fullback during the offseason of his third season. VanSumeren had originally played fullback for the first two seasons of his collegiate career and moved to linebacker during his final two. ==Early life== VanSumeren was born on May 5, 2000, and grew up in [[Bay City, Michigan]].{{Cite web|url=https://msuspartans.com/sports/football/roster/ben-vansumeren/12065|publisher=[[Michigan State Spartans]]|title=Ben VanSumeren}} By age six, he declared that he was going to be a professional football player.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2023/04/when-6-year-old-ben-vansumeren-said-he-was-nfl-bound-it-was-more-than-a-dream.html|website=[[MLive.com]]|title=When 6-year-old Ben VanSumeren said he was NFL-bound, it was more than a dream|author=Thompson, Lee|date=April 26, 2023}} He attended [[Garber High School]] in [[Essexville, Michigan|Essexville]], playing at different points [[linebacker]], [[defensive lineman]], [[quarterback]], [[running back]] and [[wide receiver]] when needed. VanSumeren played best at receiver, leading [[Bay County, Michigan|Bay County]] in receiving for three years, including a [[Senior (education)|senior]] campaign that saw him post a regular season state record 81 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 1,259 yards and 13 [[touchdowns]], being named by [[Associated Press]] the division player of the year. Although initially committing to [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]], he flipped to [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]] after receiving a late offer from them.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2017/12/meet_ben_vansumeren_michigan_f.html|website=[[MLive.com]]|title=Meet Ben VanSumeren, Michigan football's better-late-than-never signee|author=Thompson, Lee|date=December 20, 2017}} ==College career== Recruited to play [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]], VanSumeren appeared in four games for Michigan as a true [[freshman]] in 2018, preserving his [[Redshirt (sports)|redshirt]] status.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/detroit-free-press/124205215/|newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 2, 2020|page=B5|title=VanSumeren finding role on the defensive side|author=Sang, Orion}} {{Open access}} He moved to running back in 2019, playing five games with five [[Rush (gridiron football)|rushes]] for 20 yards and one touchdown. He moved to linebacker in 2020, playing six games but only posting seven [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/ben-vansumeren-lb-michigan-state-nfl-draft-scouting-report-2023/|publisher=Pro Football Network|title=Ben VanSumeren, LB, Michigan State {{!}} NFL Draft Scouting Report|author=Katz, Jason|date=April 20, 2023}} Due to his limited playing time, he transferred to the rival [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]]. In his first season at Michigan State, VanSumeren played in all 13 games, but only managed to make 12 tackles. He initially entered the transfer portal in 2022, but then opted to return to the Spartans.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2023/03/ben-vansumeren-stuck-with-michigan-state-and-it-paid-off-with-shot-at-nfl.html|website=[[MLive.com]]|title=Ben VanSumeren stuck with Michigan State and it pays off with shot at NFL|author=Wenzel, Matt|date=March 28, 2023}} In his final year, he saw his first significant playing time, starting 10 of 11 games and making 81 tackles with two [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] and two [[Pass deflected|pass breakups]]. Although VanSumeren had one year of eligibility left, he opted to accept an invitation to the [[East–West Shrine Bowl]] and declared for the [[NFL draft]]. ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 2 | weight = 231 | dash = 4.45 | ten split = 1.52 | twenty split = 2.53 | shuttle = 4.46 | cone drill = 7.10 | vertical = 42.5 | broad ft = 10 | broad in = 11 | bench = 29 | arm span = 31 | hand span = 9 1/4 | wingspan ft = 6 | wingspan in = 4 1/2 | note = All values from [[Pro Day]]{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=1022822&DraftYear=2023 |title=2023 NFL Draft Scout Ben VanSumeren College Football Profile |access-date=July 8, 2023 |website=DraftScout.com}} }} ===Philadelphia Eagles=== Despite being projected by several sources as a pick in the [[2023 NFL draft]], VanSumeren went unselected; afterwards, he was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]], being given a contract that included $130,000 guaranteed.{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/michiganstate/football/michigan-state-spartans-football-nfl-draft-pro-day-ben-vansumeren-kendall-brooks-msu-032123|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Michigan State LB Ben VanSumeren wows on-lookers at Spartans' Pro Day|date=March 21, 2023|author=Mulcrone, Aeden}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2023/04/nfl-analyst-guarantees-michigan-state-lb-ben-vansumeren-will-be-drafted.html|website=[[MLive.com]]|title=NFL analyst guarantees Michigan State LB Ben VanSumeren will be drafted|date=April 20, 2023|author=Wenzel, Matt}}{{Cite news|url=https://theeagleswire.usatoday.com/2023/05/02/philadelphia-eagles-ben-vansumeren-undrafted-rookie-free-agency-nfl-draft-guaranteed-contract-details/|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|title=Eagles' UDFA deal with Michigan State linebacker Ben VanSumeren is for $130K guaranteed|date=May 2, 2023|author=Erby, Glenn}} He was waived on August 29, and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].{{cite web|title=Eagles announce initial 53-man roster|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-2023|author1=Spadaro, Dave|author2=McPherson, Chris|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=August 29, 2023}}{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=Owen |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Eagles announce practice squad |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-practice-squad-2023 |access-date=2024-10-17 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}} Beginning on November 5, 2023, VanSumeren was called up from the practice squad for 3 consecutive weeks with his first game being against the [[Dallas Cowboys]].
